title.zh: 卷一百三十八 列傳第八十八: 趙憬 韋倫 賈耽 姜公輔
title.en: Volume 138 Biographies 88: Zhao Jing, Wei Lun, Jia Dan, Jiang Gongfu
title.raw: 卷一百三十八 列傳第八十八: 趙憬 韋倫 賈耽 姜公輔 Volume 138 Biographies 88: Zhao Jing, Wei Lun, Jia Dan, Jiang Gongfu

sentences.zh: 趙憬，字退翁，天水隴西人也。

translations.literal: Zhao Jing, styled Tuoweng, was a native of Longxi in Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Jing (styled Tuoweng) was from Longxi in Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 總章中吏部侍郎、同東西臺三品仁本之曾孫。

translations.literal: He was the great-grandson of Renben, who during the Zongzhang era had served as Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel and as Third-Rank Commissioner of the Eastern and Western Offices.
translations.idiomatic: He was the great-grandson of Renben, who in the Zongzhang period had been Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel and Co-equal Commissioner of the Third Rank for the Eastern and Western Offices.

sentences.zh: 祖諠歷左司郎中。

translations.literal: His grandfather Chan had served successively as Director of the Left Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Chan had held the post of Director in the Left Bureau.

sentences.zh: 父道先，洪州錄事參軍。

translations.literal: His father Daoxian was a Registrar Clerk in Hong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Daoxian had served as Registrar Clerk in Hongzhou.

sentences.zh: 憬少好學，誌行修潔，不求聞達。

translations.literal: When young, Jing loved study; his purpose and conduct were cultivated and pure, and he did not seek fame.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Jing devoted himself to learning; his ambitions and conduct were scrupulous, and he sought no renown.

sentences.zh: 寶應中，玄宗、肅宗梓宮未祔，有司議山陵制度。

translations.literal: In the Baoying era the spirit tablets of Xuanzong and Suzong had not yet been enshrined together, and the relevant offices deliberated on the regulations for the imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: During the Baoying era, Xuanzong's and Suzong's remains had not yet been laid in the imperial tombs, and the authorities debated the proper ceremonial arrangements.

sentences.zh: 時西蕃入寇，天下饑饉，憬以褐衣上疏，宜遵儉制，時人稱之。

translations.literal: At that time the Western Tibetans invaded, the realm suffered famine, and Jing in commoner's garb submitted a memorial urging adherence to frugal standards; people of the time praised him.
translations.idiomatic: With Tibetans raiding the west and famine spreading across the empire, Jing submitted a memorial in plain dress calling for strict economy in the tomb project, earning widespread praise.

sentences.zh: 後連為州從事，試江夏尉。

translations.literal: Later he served in succession as a provincial aide and was tested as Warden of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to serve as aide in several prefectures and was appointed acting magistrate of Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 累遷監察御史，隨牒籓府，歷殿中侍御史、太子舍人。

translations.literal: He was promoted repeatedly to Supervising Censor, followed his credentials to a frontier commissionerate, and held successively the posts of Attending Censor within the Palace and Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Rising to Supervising Censor, he served on a frontier commissionerate staff and later became Palace Attending Censor and Mentor in the Heir Apparent's household.

sentences.zh: 居母憂，哀毀幾絕。

translations.literal: While observing mourning for his mother, his grief and emaciation nearly cost him his life.
translations.idiomatic: During mourning for his mother, his grief was so severe that he nearly died from it.

sentences.zh: 服除，建中初，擢授水部員外郎。

translations.literal: When his mourning ended, in the early Jianzhong era he was selected and appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period, in the early Jianzhong period he was promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 未拜，會湖南觀察使李承請為副使、檢校工部郎中，充職。

translations.literal: Before he could assume the post, the Military Governor of Hunan, Li Cheng, requested him as deputy commissioner and Acting Director of the Ministry of Works, and he took up those duties.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take office, Li Cheng, Military Governor of Hunan, asked to have him as deputy and Acting Director of the Ministry of Works, and he served in that capacity.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，承卒，遂知留後事。

translations.literal: After more than a year Cheng died, and Jing then managed the affairs of the acting military governorship.
translations.idiomatic: A year later Cheng died, and Jing assumed charge of the governorship as acting commander.

sentences.zh: 尋授潭州刺史、兼御史中丞、湖南觀察使，仍賜金紫。

translations.literal: He was soon appointed Prefect of Tanzhou, concurrently Censor-in-Chief and Military Governor of Hunan, and was also granted the gold-purple insignia.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was made Prefect of Tan, concurrently Censor-in-Chief and Military Governor of Hunan, and was awarded the gold-and-purple regalia.

sentences.zh: 居二歲，受代歸京師，闔門靜居，不與人交。

translations.literal: After two years he was relieved and returned to the capital; he kept his household in quiet seclusion and did not associate with others.
translations.idiomatic: After two years he was replaced and returned to the capital, where he lived quietly at home and kept company with no one.

sentences.zh: 久之，特召對於別殿。

translations.literal: After a long while he was specially summoned for an audience in a separate hall.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was specially summoned to an audience in a side hall.

sentences.zh: 憬多學問，有辭辯，敷奏稱旨，上悅，拜給事中。

translations.literal: Jing was widely learned and eloquent; his presentations pleased the emperor, who was delighted and appointed him Drafting Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was learned and articulate; his presentations at court pleased the emperor, who appointed him Drafting Attendant.

sentences.zh: 貞元四年，回紇請結和親。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenyuan the Uyghurs requested a marriage alliance.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhenyuan (788) the Uyghurs sought a marriage alliance.

sentences.zh: 詔以鹹安公主降回紇，命檢校右僕射關播充使。

translations.literal: An edict sent Princess Xian'an to marry into the Uyghur state and ordered the Acting Right Vice Director Guan Bo to serve as envoy.
translations.idiomatic: The court decreed that Princess Xian'an be given in marriage to the Uyghurs and appointed Acting Right Vice Director Guan Bo chief envoy.

sentences.zh: 憬以本官兼御史中丞為副。

translations.literal: Jing in his regular office concurrently served as Censor-in-Chief as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Jing served as deputy envoy in his regular post, concurrently as Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 前後使回紇者，多私賫繒絮，蕃中市馬回以規利。

translations.literal: Envoys who had gone to the Uyghurs before often privately carried silks and floss to trade for horses in the foreign markets for profit.
translations.idiomatic: Previous envoys to the Uyghurs had often carried private loads of silk to trade for horses at the frontier markets for personal gain.

sentences.zh: 憬一無所市，人嘆美之。

translations.literal: Jing purchased nothing at all, and people praised him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Jing bought nothing on the journey, and the public admired him for it.

sentences.zh: 使還，遷尚書左丞，綱轄省務，清勤奉職。

translations.literal: On his return he was promoted to Left Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue and oversaw the affairs of the ministry with diligence and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned he was promoted to Left Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue, where he managed departmental affairs with scrupulous diligence.

sentences.zh: 竇參為宰相，惡其能，請出為同州刺史，上不從。

translations.literal: Dou Can was chief minister and disliked Jing's ability; he asked that Jing be sent out as Prefect of Tongzhou, but the emperor did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Dou Can, resenting Jing's talent, asked that he be sent out as Prefect of Tongzhou, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 八年四月，竇參罷黜，憬與陸贄並拜中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the eighth year Dou Can was dismissed, and Jing together with Lu Zhi were appointed Vice Directors of the Secretariat and Fellows of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the eighth year (792) Dou Can was removed from office, and Jing and Lu Zhi were both made Vice Directors of the Secretariat and Grand Councilors.

sentences.zh: 憬深於理道，常言：「為政之本，在於選賢能，務節儉，薄賦斂，寬刑罰。

translations.literal: Jing was deeply versed in principle and the Way, and often said: 'The root of government lies in selecting the worthy and capable, practicing economy, lightening taxes and levies, and moderating punishments.'
translations.idiomatic: Jing was steeped in statecraft and often said that the foundation of rule lay in choosing able men, practicing frugality, easing tax burdens, and tempering punishments.

sentences.zh: 」對揚之際，必以此為言，乃獻《審官六議》曰：

translations.literal: Whenever he responded to the emperor's questions he always spoke on these themes, and then presented his 'Six Discussions on Examining Officials.'
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he addressed the throne he returned to these themes, and he submitted his 'Six Discussions on Examining Officials.'

sentences.zh: 臣謬登宰府，四年於茲，恭承德音，未嘗不以求賢為切。

translations.literal: Your servant has wrongly ascended to the chief minister's seat and has been there four years now; respectfully receiving your virtuous instructions, I have never failed to make seeking the worthy my urgent concern.
translations.idiomatic: I have held a seat in the council for four years now; receiving Your Majesty's enlightened guidance, I have always made the search for talent my foremost duty.

sentences.zh: 至於延薦，職在愚臣，雖當代天之工，且乏知人之鑒；

translations.literal: As for extending recommendations, that duty rests on your foolish servant; though I bear the work of the age, I lack the discernment to know men.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the duty of recommending men falls to me; though I bear the burdens of the age, I lack the eye to judge character.

sentences.zh: 漸積歲月，負於聖明，無補王猷，有妨賢路。

translations.literal: Month by month I have accumulated failures against the sage brilliance, done nothing to aid the royal plan, and obstructed the path of the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Month after month I have fallen short of Your Majesty's expectations, contributed nothing to state policy, and blocked the way for able men.

sentences.zh: 況多疾恙，兼慮闕遺，頃奉表章，備陳肝膈。

translations.literal: Moreover I suffer many illnesses and fear omissions as well; recently I submitted a memorial setting forth my inmost thoughts.
translations.idiomatic: I am moreover afflicted with many ailments and fear I have overlooked much; I recently submitted a memorial laying bare my heart.

sentences.zh: 陛下以臣性拙直，身病可矜，不棄孱微，尚加委任。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, seeing that your servant's nature is blunt and upright and that my illness deserves pity, did not abandon this feeble man but still added to my commission.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, seeing my blunt honesty and pitying my illness, did not cast me aside but continued to entrust me with office.

sentences.zh: 自此思省，報效尤難，莫副堯、舜之心，空懷屍素之懼。

translations.literal: Since then I have reflected and found repayment of favor especially difficult; I cannot match the hearts of Yao and Shun and can only harbor the fear of holding office in vain.
translations.idiomatic: Since then I have reflected that it is all the harder to repay your grace; I cannot equal the sages Yao and Shun, and I live in dread of occupying my post without merit.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下法象應期，聖神廣運，雲行雨施，皆發自然，訓誥典謨，悉經睿覽。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that Your Majesty's pattern corresponds to the seasons, your sage spirit extends far, cloud and rain move of themselves, all arising naturally; your instructions and classical models have all passed before your wise perusal.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's rule answers to the seasons, your sacred intelligence ranges far and wide; your beneficent acts flow as naturally as rain from clouds, and every edict and classic model has received your sage scrutiny.

sentences.zh: 臣所以不敢援引古昔，上煩天聰，且以用人之要，願伸鄙見。

translations.literal: Your servant therefore dares not cite antiquity to trouble heaven's hearing, but wishes to set forth a humble view on the essentials of employing men.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore dare not weary Your Majesty with citations from antiquity, but wish to offer a modest view on what matters in the appointment of officials.

sentences.zh: 復念稽顙丹陛，仰對宸嚴，謇訥易窮，遽數難辯，理詳則塵瀆頗甚，言略則利害未宣。

translations.literal: I also recall bowing on the cinnabar steps and looking up at the imperial countenance: stammering is soon exhausted, and hurried enumeration is hard to argue; if the reasoning is detailed the dust of importunity becomes excessive, if the words are brief then benefit and harm are not made clear.
translations.idiomatic: I recall too how, prostrate on the palace steps and facing the throne, halting speech soon fails and hasty listing is hard to follow; if I am thorough I weary Your Majesty, if I am brief I leave the stakes unclear.

sentences.zh: 若默以求容，茍而竊位，縱天地之仁幸免，而中外之責何逃！

translations.literal: If I seek acceptance by silence or cling to office by compromise, even if heaven and earth's kindness spared me, how could I escape blame within and without!
translations.idiomatic: If I sought only to please by silence or clung to office unworthily, even heaven's mercy might spare me, but how could I escape censure at court and in the provinces!

sentences.zh: 非陛下用臣之意也。

translations.literal: That is not Your Majesty's intent in employing your servant.
translations.idiomatic: That is not why Your Majesty keeps me in office.

sentences.zh: 其所欲言者，皆陛下聖慮之內。

translations.literal: What I wish to say lies entirely within Your Majesty's sacred deliberations.
translations.idiomatic: What I mean to say is already within Your Majesty's own sage understanding.

sentences.zh: 臣以頂戴恩造，不知所為，身被風毒，漸覺沈痼，是以勤勤懇懇，切於愚誠也。

translations.literal: Your servant, bearing your gracious creation on my head, knows not what to do; my body has been struck by wind toxins and I feel my illness growing heavy—hence my earnest, earnest pleading springs from sincere foolishness.
translations.idiomatic: Bearing Your Majesty's grace upon my head, I scarcely know what to do; wind toxins afflict my body and my illness grows worse—hence this earnest plea from an honest but limited man.

sentences.zh: 臣聞貞觀、開元之際，宰輔論事，或多上書，所冀獲盡情理。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that in the Zhenguan and Kaiyuan eras, when chief ministers discussed affairs, many submitted written memorials, hoping thereby to set forth the full circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenguan and Kaiyuan periods, chief ministers often memorialized in writing when they discussed policy, so that every aspect of a question could be laid out.

sentences.zh: 今臣酌前代之損益，體當時之通變，謹獻《審官六議》，伏惟閑宴時賜省覽。

translations.literal: Now your servant has weighed the gains and losses of former ages and adapted to the needs of the present, and respectfully presents the 'Six Discussions on Examining Officials,' humbly asking that Your Majesty peruse them at leisure.
translations.idiomatic: I have now weighed the lessons of earlier dynasties against the needs of our own time and respectfully submit the 'Six Discussions,' begging Your Majesty to read them at your leisure.

sentences.zh: 其大指，議相，則曰：「宜博采眾賢，用為輔弼。

translations.literal: Its main import, in discussing the chief minister, says: 'One should broadly gather the many worthy and use them as assistants.'
translations.idiomatic: On the chief minister, its gist is this: 'The throne should draw widely on worthy men and employ them as counselors.'

sentences.zh: 今中外知其賢者，伏願陛下用之，識其能者任之，求其全材，恐不可得。」

translations.literal: Those whom court and countryside know to be worthy—your servant humbly hopes Your Majesty will employ them; recognize those with ability and assign them duties; to seek a man of complete talent is perhaps impossible.'
translations.idiomatic: For every man known at court or in the provinces to be worthy, I beg Your Majesty to use him; recognize ability and assign office; to demand a flawless candidate may be impossible.'

sentences.zh: 議進用庶官，則曰：「異同之論，是非難辨。

translations.literal: In discussing the promotion and employment of ordinary officials, it says: 'When opinions differ, right and wrong are hard to distinguish.'
translations.idiomatic: On promoting ordinary officials, it says: 'Where opinions clash, merit and fault are hard to tell apart.'

sentences.zh: 由考課難於實效，好惡雜於眾聲，所以訪之彌多，得之彌少。

translations.literal: Because examination of performance is hard to make real and likes and dislikes mingle in the clamor of many voices, the more one inquires the more one asks, the less one obtains.
translations.idiomatic: Because performance reviews rarely match reality and private likes and dislikes color public rumor, the more one investigates, the fewer true men one finds.

sentences.zh: 選士古今為難，拔十得五，賢愚猶半。

translations.literal: Selecting scholars has been difficult in every age; to pick ten and get five, worthy and foolish are still half and half.
translations.idiomatic: Choosing officials has always been hard; even if one in ten proves sound, worthy and unworthy may still be evenly mixed.

sentences.zh: 陛下謂臣曰：『何必五也？

translations.literal: Your Majesty said to your servant: 'Why must it be five?'
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty once said to me: 'Why insist on half?'

sentences.zh: 十得二三斯可矣！

translations.literal: To obtain two or three out of ten would suffice!'
translations.idiomatic: If two or three in ten are sound, that is enough!'

sentences.zh: 』聖主思賢至是，而宰臣不能進之，臣之罪也。

translations.literal: The sage ruler's longing for the worthy reaches even to this, yet the chief minister cannot advance them—the fault is your servant's.'
translations.idiomatic: When the Son of Heaven longs for talent to this degree yet his chief minister cannot supply it, the fault is mine.'

sentences.zh: 進賢在於廣任用，明殿最，舉大節，棄其小瑕，隨其所能，試之以事，用人之大綱也。」

translations.literal: Advancing the worthy lies in broadening appointments, clarifying grades of achievement, honoring great principles, overlooking small faults, following each man's capacity, and testing him in office—this is the great outline of employing men.'
translations.idiomatic: To advance talent one must appoint widely, judge by major achievements, prize great integrity, overlook minor flaws, assign men according to capacity, and test them in office—that is the broad policy of appointment.'

sentences.zh: 議京諸司闕官，則曰：「當今要官多闕，閑官十無一二。

translations.literal: In discussing vacancies among the capital offices, it says: 'At present many important posts stand empty, while idle posts are fewer than one in ten.'
translations.idiomatic: On vacancies in the capital ministries, it says: 'Today many key posts are unfilled, while sinecures number scarcely one in ten.'

sentences.zh: 文武任用，資序遞遷，要官本以材行，閑官多由恩澤。

translations.literal: Civil and military appointments advance by seniority in rank; important posts should rest on talent and conduct, while idle posts are mostly filled by favor.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officers rise by seniority; important posts ought to go by ability and character, but idle posts are largely filled by patronage.

sentences.zh: 朝廷或將任，多擬要官則人少闕多，閑官則人多闕少；

translations.literal: When the court is about to make an appointment, if it plans for an important post there are few men and many vacancies, but if for an idle post there are many men and few vacancies.
translations.idiomatic: When the court prepares an appointment, naming an important post leaves few candidates for many vacancies, while naming a sinecure leaves many candidates for few openings.

sentences.zh: 明當選拔者轉少，在優容者轉多，宜補闕員，務育材用。

translations.literal: Those clearly fit for selection grow fewer, while those merely tolerated grow more; vacant posts should be filled and talent nurtured for use.
translations.idiomatic: Men clearly qualified for promotion grow fewer, while those merely indulged grow more; vacancies should be filled and talent cultivated for service.

sentences.zh: 大廈永固，是棟梁榱桷之全也；

translations.literal: A great mansion stands forever because beams, ridgepoles, rafters, and brackets are all complete.
translations.idiomatic: A great hall endures because every beam, rafter, and bracket is in place.

sentences.zh: 聖朝致理，亦庶官群吏之能也。」

translations.literal: When the sacred dynasty attains good order, it likewise depends on the ability of the many officials and clerks.'
translations.idiomatic: When the dynasty achieves good government, it likewise rests on the capacity of the whole corps of officials.'

sentences.zh: 議中外考課官，則曰：「漢以數易長吏，謂之弊政。

translations.literal: In discussing examining officials within and without the capital, it says: 'Under Han they frequently changed long-term magistrates, which was called a defective policy.'
translations.idiomatic: On performance review for capital and provincial officials, it says: 'The Han often replaced long-serving local magistrates, which was regarded as a flawed practice.'

sentences.zh: 其有能理者，輒增秩賜金，或八九年、十余年，乃入為九卿，或遷三輔。

translations.literal: When there were those who could govern well, they would at once raise rank and bestow gold; some after eight or nine years, or more than ten, would enter the Nine Ministers, or be transferred to the Three Metropolises.
translations.idiomatic: When a man governed well, they promptly raised his rank and granted gold; some after eight, nine, or more than ten years entered the Nine Ministers or were moved to the metropolitan districts.

sentences.zh: 功績茂異，遂至丞相，其間不隔數官。

translations.literal: If his achievements and virtue were outstandingly abundant, he might reach the post of chief minister, with no more than a few offices intervening.
translations.idiomatic: Men of outstanding achievement could rise even to chief minister without many steps between.

sentences.zh: 今陛下內選庶僚，外委州府，課績高者，不次超升，致理之法，無逾於此。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty selects subordinates within and entrusts prefectures without; those of high performance are promoted out of turn—no method of achieving order surpasses this.
translations.idiomatic: Today Your Majesty chooses subordinates at court and delegates the provinces; those with outstanding records are promoted ahead of schedule—no better method of good government exists.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為黜陟且立年限，若所居要重，未當遷移，就加爵秩。

translations.literal: Your servant foolishly thinks that dismissal and promotion should also set term limits; if one holds an important post and ought not yet to be moved, let rank and title be added instead.
translations.idiomatic: I would add that promotion and demotion should follow fixed terms; if a man holds a crucial post and should not yet be transferred, let his rank and title be increased in place.

sentences.zh: 其余進退，令知褒貶之必應，遲速之有常。

translations.literal: For the rest, in advancement and withdrawal let men know that praise and blame will surely follow, and that delay and haste have their constants.
translations.idiomatic: For all others, let advancement and retirement proceed so that men know reward and censure will follow, and that pace has its rule.

sentences.zh: 如課績在中，年考及限，與之平轉。

translations.literal: If performance falls in the middle and the annual review reaches its term, give him a regular transfer.
translations.idiomatic: If a man's review is middling and his term is complete, transfer him in the ordinary course.

sentences.zh: 中外叠處，歷試其能，使無茍且之心，又無滯淹之慮。」

translations.literal: Within and without, in successive posts, test his ability, so that there is neither a heart of make-do nor the worry of long stagnation.'
translations.idiomatic: Let him serve in successive posts at court and in the provinces, testing his ability, so that he neither grows complacent nor languishes in place.'

sentences.zh: 議舉遺滯，則曰：「官司既廣，必委宰輔以舉之；

translations.literal: In discussing recommending the overlooked and stagnant, it says: 'Since government offices are broad, one must entrust chief ministers to recommend men.'
translations.idiomatic: On recommending overlooked talent, it says: 'Because the bureaucracy is vast, the throne must rely on chief ministers to nominate men.'

sentences.zh: 宰輔不能遍知，又詢於庶官；

translations.literal: Chief ministers cannot know everyone; they also inquire of ordinary officials.
translations.idiomatic: Chief ministers cannot know every candidate; they must also consult lower officials.

sentences.zh: 庶官不能遍知，又訪於眾人。

translations.literal: Ordinary officials cannot know everyone either; they also ask the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Lower officials cannot know everyone either; they turn to wider opinion.

sentences.zh: 眾聲囂然，互有臧否，十人舉之未信，一人毀之可疑，迨至於今，茲弊未改。

translations.literal: The clamor of many voices, each with praise or blame; ten men recommend and it is not yet believed, one man slanders and doubt arises—to this day this abuse has not been reformed.
translations.idiomatic: Public rumor swells with conflicting praise and blame; ten recommendations still fail to convince, one slander raises doubt—and to this day the abuse persists.

sentences.zh: 其所以然者，非盡為愛憎也，苦於不審實而承聲言之。

translations.literal: The reason is not wholly personal love and hate; the hardship lies in not verifying facts and repeating what one has merely heard.
translations.idiomatic: The cause is not always personal favor or spite; men repeat hearsay because facts are never verified.

sentences.zh: 大凡常人之心，以稱人之善為清，以攻人之過為直，茍有除授，多生橫議。

translations.literal: As a rule the heart of ordinary men takes praising another's goodness as purity and attacking another's fault as uprightness; whenever there is a new appointment, many raise reckless objections.
translations.idiomatic: Ordinary men think it refined to praise others and blunt to attack their faults; whenever a new appointment is made, reckless objections multiply.

sentences.zh: 由是宰臣每將薦用，亦自重難，日往月來，未副聖意。

translations.literal: Hence whenever chief ministers are about to recommend someone, they also feel the weight of difficulty; day after day and month after month they fail to satisfy the sage intent.
translations.idiomatic: Hence chief ministers hesitate before recommending anyone; day after day they fall short of Your Majesty's intent.

sentences.zh: 宜須采聽時論，以所舉多者先用，必非大故，皆不棄之。」

translations.literal: One should gather and listen to opinion of the time and employ first those most often recommended; unless the fault is grave, none should be abandoned.'
translations.idiomatic: The court should heed current opinion and appoint first those most widely recommended; unless the fault is grave, no nominee should be cast aside.'

sentences.zh: 議擢用諸使府僚屬，則曰：「諸使辟吏，各自精求，務於得人，將重府望。

translations.literal: In discussing promoting staff from the various commissionerates, it says: 'When the various commissioners recruit clerks, each carefully seeks men, striving to obtain talent and thereby enhance the prestige of the office.'
translations.idiomatic: On promoting staff from military commissionerates, it says: 'Each commissioner recruits his own staff with care, seeking able men to strengthen his headquarters.'

sentences.zh: 既經試效，能否可知，擢其賢能，置之朝列。

translations.literal: Once they have been tested in office, ability and inability are known; promote the worthy and capable and place them in the court ranks.
translations.idiomatic: After trial in office their merit is known; raise the able among them to posts at court.

sentences.zh: 或曰外使須才，固不可奪。

translations.literal: Some say the outer commissioners need talent and therefore men cannot be taken away.
translations.idiomatic: Some object that frontier commissioners need talent and must not be stripped of staff.

sentences.zh: 臣知必不然也。

translations.literal: Your servant knows this is surely not so.
translations.idiomatic: I know that is not so.

sentences.zh: 屬者使府賓介，每有登朝，本使殊以為榮，自喜知人，且明公選。

translations.literal: In recent times when staff from commissionerates entered the court, their original commissioner especially took it as an honor, pleased that he knew men and that public selection was clear.
translations.idiomatic: When commissionerate staff entered court service, their former chief took pride in it, glad to have recognized talent and to see the public selection vindicated.

sentences.zh: 大凡才能之士，名位未達，多在方鎮。

translations.literal: As a rule men of ability whose fame and rank have not yet risen are mostly in the regional commands.
translations.idiomatic: As a rule, able men whose names have not yet risen are found chiefly in the provinces.

sentences.zh: 日月在上，誰不知之，思登闕庭，如望霄漢，宜須博采，無宜久滯。

translations.literal: The sun and moon are above—who does not know it? They long to ascend the palace court as if gazing at the Milky Way; one should gather broadly and not let them linger long.'
translations.idiomatic: The throne shines as the sun and moon—who does not see it? They yearn for court as men gaze at the heavens; the court should gather them widely and not leave them long in the provinces.'

sentences.zh: 」上優詔答之。

translations.literal: The emperor replied with an excellent edict.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor responded with a gracious edict of approval.

sentences.zh: 時吏部侍郎杜黃裳為中貴讒譖及他過犯，御史中丞穆贊、京兆少尹韋武、萬年縣令李宣、長安令盧雲，皆為裴延齡構陷，將加斥逐。

translations.literal: At that time Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel Du Huangxiang was slandered by inner eunuchs and implicated in other offenses; Censor-in-Chief Mu Zan, Junior Vice Director of the Metropolitan Prefecture Wei Wu, Magistrate of Wannian Li Xuan, and Magistrate of Chang'an Lu Yun were all framed by Pei Yanling and were about to be driven out.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Du Huangxiang, Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel, was slandered by palace eunuchs and charged with other offenses; Censor-in-Chief Mu Zan, Junior Vice Director of the Metropolitan Prefecture Wei Wu, Magistrate of Wannian Li Xuan, and Magistrate of Chang'an Lu Yun were all framed by Pei Yanling and faced dismissal.

sentences.zh: 憬保護救解之，故多從輕貶。

translations.literal: Jing protected them and secured their release, so most received only light demotion.
translations.idiomatic: Jing intervened to protect them, so most received only mild demotion.

sentences.zh: 初，憬廉察湖南，令狐峘、崔儆並為巡屬刺史。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Jing inspected Hunan, Linghu Yan and Cui Yi had both served as touring prefects under him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Jing served as inspector of Hunan, Linghu Yan and Cui Yi had both been touring prefects on his staff.

sentences.zh: 峘嘗歷中書舍人、禮部侍郎，儆久在朝列，所為或虧法令，憬每以正道制之。

translations.literal: Yan had once been Drafting Attendant and Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites; Yi had long been in the court ranks; when their conduct sometimes fell short of law, Jing always restrained them by the upright path.
translations.idiomatic: Yan had served as Drafting Attendant and Vice Director of Rites; Yi had long held court office; when either overstepped the law, Jing checked him with upright counsel.

sentences.zh: 峘、儆密遣人數憬罪狀，毀之於朝。

translations.literal: Yan and Yi secretly sent men several times to report Jing's offenses and slandered him at court.
translations.idiomatic: Yan and Yi secretly sent men to denounce Jing repeatedly and slandered him at court.

sentences.zh: 及憬為相，拔儆自大理卿為尚書右丞，峘先貶官為別駕，又擢為吉州刺史，時人多之。

translations.literal: When Jing became chief minister he promoted Yi from Director of the Court of Judicial Review to Right Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue; Yan, who had earlier been demoted to an assistant post, was also raised to Prefect of Ji; people of the time praised this.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing became chief minister he raised Yi from Director of Judicial Review to Right Vice Director of Revenue, and Yan, though earlier demoted, to Prefect of Ji—acts widely praised.

sentences.zh: 憬與陸贄同知政事。

translations.literal: Jing together with Lu Zhi jointly managed government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Jing and Lu Zhi shared governmental authority.

sentences.zh: 贄恃久在禁庭，特承恩顧，以國政為己任，才周歲，轉憬為門下侍郎。

translations.literal: Zhi, relying on his long service within the palace precincts, especially received imperial favor and took state affairs as his own responsibility; within a full year he transferred Jing to Vice Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi, having long served in the inner palace, enjoyed special favor and treated state affairs as his own charge; within a year he moved Jing to Vice Director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 憬由是深銜之，數以目疾請告，不甚當政事，因是不相協。

translations.literal: Jing therefore bore a deep resentment; several times he pleaded eye illness and took leave, seldom attending to government, and for this reason they did not cooperate.
translations.idiomatic: Jing deeply resented this; he repeatedly pleaded eye trouble and stayed away from office, so the two ceased to work in harmony.

sentences.zh: 裴延齡奸詐恣睢，滿朝側目。

translations.literal: Pei Yanling was treacherous, deceitful, and overbearing; the whole court looked askance at him.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yanling was cunning, fraudulent, and domineering; the entire court watched him with distaste.

sentences.zh: 憬初與贄約於上前論之，及延英奏對，贄極言延齡奸邪誑誕之狀，不可任用。

translations.literal: Jing at first agreed with Zhi to debate him before the emperor; when they presented themselves at the Yanchi Hall for imperial questioning, Zhi spoke at length on Yanling's treacherous, deceitful, and delusive conduct and that he could not be employed.
translations.idiomatic: Jing had first agreed with Zhi to denounce Yanling before the emperor; at the Yanchi audience Zhi spoke at length of Yanling's fraud and insisted he must not be employed.

sentences.zh: 德宗不悅，形於顏色。

translations.literal: Dezong was displeased and showed it in his countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong was displeased, and his displeasure showed on his face.

sentences.zh: 憬默然無言，由是罷贄平章事，而憬當國矣。

translations.literal: Jing was silent and said nothing; for this reason Zhi was removed from the post of Grand Councilor, and Jing then held the government alone.
translations.idiomatic: Jing remained silent; for this Zhi was dismissed as Grand Councilor, and Jing alone directed the government.

sentences.zh: 時宰相賈耽、盧邁與憬三人。

translations.literal: At that time the chief ministers Jia Dan, Lu Mai, and Jing were three.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the chief ministers were Jia Dan, Lu Mai, and Jing.

sentences.zh: 十二年春正月，耽、邁皆有假，故憬獨對於延英。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring in the twelfth year Dan and Mai both took leave, so Jing alone responded at the Yanchi Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the twelfth year (796) Dan and Mai were both on leave, so Jing alone faced the emperor at Yanchi.

sentences.zh: 上問曰：「近日起居註記何事？

translations.literal: The emperor asked: 'What affairs have the recent Daily Records noted?'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked: 'What have the Daily Records recorded of late?'

sentences.zh: 」憬對曰：「古者左史記言，人君動止，有實言隨即記錄，起居註是也。

translations.literal: Jing replied: 'In antiquity the left historiographer recorded words; the ruler's movements and stops—whatever was actually spoken was at once recorded; such is the Daily Record.'
translations.idiomatic: Jing answered: 'In antiquity the left historiographer recorded the ruler's words; whatever the sovereign actually said was entered at once—that is the Daily Record.'

sentences.zh: 國朝永徽中，起居唯得對仗承旨，仗下後謀議皆不得聞，其記註唯編制敕，更無他事。

translations.literal: In our dynasty, in the Yonghui era, the Daily Record attendants might only receive instructions during the imperial audience; after the audience all deliberations could not be heard, and the record noted only the drafting of edicts, with nothing else.
translations.idiomatic: Under our dynasty, from the Yonghui period onward, recorders heard only what was announced during formal audiences; deliberations afterward went unrecorded, and the Daily Record compiled only edicts, with no other business.

sentences.zh: 所以長壽中姚璹知政事，以為親承德音謨訓，若不宣旨，宰相、史官無以得書。

translations.literal: Therefore in the Changshou era, when Yao Chong knew government affairs, he held that since he personally received the virtuous sounds and instructions, if the emperor did not proclaim them, the chief ministers and historiographers had no means to write them down.
translations.idiomatic: Hence in the Changshou period, when Yao Chong held power, he argued that because he personally received the emperor's instructions, unless they were proclaimed, chief ministers and historiographers could not record them.

sentences.zh: 璹請宰相一人記錄所論軍國政事，謂之時政記，每月送史館。

translations.literal: Chong requested that one chief minister record the military and state affairs discussed, calling it the Current-Affairs Record, to be sent monthly to the History Office.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chong asked that a chief minister record deliberations on military and civil affairs in a "Current-Affairs Record" sent monthly to the Historiography Office.

sentences.zh: 既而時政記又廢。

translations.literal: Before long the Current-Affairs Record was again abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the practice was abandoned again.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「君舉必書，義存勸誡。

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'The ruler's actions must be written down; the meaning lies in encouragement and warning.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "A ruler's acts must be recorded—that is how admonition and example are preserved."

sentences.zh: 既嘗有時政記，宰臣宜依故事為之。

translations.literal: Since there had once been a Current-Affairs Record, the chief ministers ought to follow precedent in making one.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Current-Affairs Record had existed before, the chief ministers should revive it according to precedent.

sentences.zh: 」無何，憬卒，時政記亦不行。

translations.literal: Before long Jing died, and the Current-Affairs Record was not carried out either.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Jing died, and the Current-Affairs Record was never implemented.

sentences.zh: 憬特承恩顧，性清儉，雖為宰輔，居第仆使，類貧士大夫之家，所得俸入，先置私廟，而竟不立第舍田產。

translations.literal: Jing especially received imperial favor; his nature was pure and frugal; though he was chief minister, his residence's servants and attendants resembled those of poor scholar-official households; the salary he received he first placed in his private ancestral temple, and in the end he never established a mansion or field property.
translations.idiomatic: Jing enjoyed special imperial favor yet lived plainly; though a chief minister, his household staff resembled a poor scholar's; he devoted his salary first to his family shrine and never built a mansion or acquired estates.

sentences.zh: 其年八月，遇暴疾，信宿而卒，時年六十一。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of that year he suffered a sudden illness and died within a day and night, aged sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of that year he fell suddenly ill and died within two days, at the age of sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 子元亮進憬遺表草曰：「臣叨荷聖慈，竊塵臺鼎，年序頗久，績用無聞，負乘之敗已彰，覆餗之咎俄及。

translations.literal: His son Yuanliang submitted Jing's draft memorial, saying: 'Your servant has presumptuously borne sacred kindness and secretly dusted the council seat; my years in office have been long and my achievements unheard of; the failure of one who cannot bear his load is already manifest, and the fault of overturning the stew is suddenly upon me.'
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuanliang presented Jing's draft memorial: "I have undeservedly held a seat at court for many years without merit; my failures are plain, and calamity has overtaken me."

sentences.zh: 而天與之疾，福過生災，自今日卯時以來，稍加困重，針灸不及，藥餌奚施。

translations.literal: Yet heaven bestowed this illness; when blessing passes, disaster is born; from the hour of mao today the affliction has grown heavier; acupuncture and moxibustion cannot reach it, and what use are medicines?
translations.idiomatic: Heaven has sent this illness; since the hour of mao today my condition has worsened; neither needle nor drug avails.

sentences.zh: 奄然遊魂，終當就木，冥冥殘喘，豈忍辭天！

translations.literal: Suddenly the wandering soul must soon go to the coffin; in the dark the lingering breath—how can I bear to leave heaven!
translations.idiomatic: My spirit must soon depart; how can I bear to leave Your Majesty's grace!

sentences.zh: 號呼涕零，側息心斷，反風結草，誓報深恩，雖死猶生，豈孤素願。

translations.literal: Crying out, weeping, and with side heaving and heart broken, I pray that returning wind and knotted grass may repay deep kindness; though I die I am as if alive—how could I betray my lifelong wish?
translations.idiomatic: I weep and call upon heaven, praying that even in death I may repay your deep kindness and not betray my lifelong devotion.

sentences.zh: 無任感恩，嗚咽痛恨之至。

translations.literal: Unable to bear my gratitude—sob and bitter regret to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: I cannot express my gratitude and grief.

sentences.zh: 」德宗尤悼惜之，廢朝三日，冊贈太子太傅，賻帛五百端、米粟四百石，令鴻臚卿王權充冊吊使。

translations.literal: Dezong especially mourned him, suspended court for three days, enfeoffed him posthumously as Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, granted five hundred bolts of silk and four hundred shi of grain and millet, and ordered the Director of the Court for Diplomatic Relations Wang Quan to serve as envoy for the enfeoffment and condolence.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong mourned him deeply, closed court for three days, posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, granted five hundred bolts of silk and four hundred shi of grain, and sent Director Wang Quan as condolence envoy.

sentences.zh: 元亮官至左司郎中、侍御史知雜事卒。

translations.literal: Yuanliang reached the post of Director of the Left Bureau and died while serving as Attending Censor with charge of miscellaneous matters.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanliang rose to Director of the Left Bureau and died while serving as Attending Censor in charge of miscellaneous matters.

sentences.zh: 次子全亮，官至侍御史、桂管防禦判官。

translations.literal: The second son Quanliang reached the post of Attending Censor and Defense Judge of Guiguan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: The second son Quanliang became Attending Censor and Defense Judge on the Guiguan staff.

sentences.zh: 元亮兄宣亮、弟承亮，皆以門廕授官。

translations.literal: Yuanliang's elder brother Xuanliang and younger brother Chengliang all received office through hereditary privilege.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanliang's elder brother Xuanliang and younger brother Chengliang all entered office by hereditary privilege.

sentences.zh: 韋倫，開元、天寶中朔方節度使光乘之子。

translations.literal: Wei Lun was the son of Guangcheng, Military Governor of Shuofang in the Kaiyuan and Tianbao eras.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Lun was the son of Guangcheng, Military Governor of Shuofang under Xuanzong.

sentences.zh: 少以廕累授藍田縣尉。

translations.literal: When young he received office through accumulated privilege as Warden of Lantian.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he received office by privilege as magistrate of Lantian.

sentences.zh: 以吏事勤恪，楊國忠署為鑄錢內作使判官。

translations.literal: Because of diligent and earnest performance of clerical duties, Yang Guozhong appointed him judge on the staff of the Inner Coinage Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: For diligent service in clerical work, Yang Guozhong appointed him judge on the Inner Coinage Commission.

sentences.zh: 國忠恃權寵，又邀名稱，多征諸州縣農人令鑄錢。

translations.literal: Guozhong relied on power and favor and also sought a reputation; he widely conscripted farmers from the various prefectures and counties to cast coin.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong abused his power and sought renown by conscripting farmers from many prefectures to cast coin.

sentences.zh: 農夫既非本色工匠，被所由抑令就役，多遭箠罰，人不聊生。

translations.literal: The farmers were not professional artisans by trade; pressed by the local authorities to take service, many suffered beating and flogging, and people could not sustain life.
translations.idiomatic: These men were not trained artisans; forced into service by local officials, many were beaten, and the people were driven to destitution.

sentences.zh: 倫白國忠曰：「鑄錢須得本色人，今抑百姓農人為之，尤費力無功，人且興謗。

translations.literal: Lun told Guozhong: 'Casting coin requires men of the proper trade; now pressing common farmers to do it is especially laborious without result, and people will raise slander.'
translations.idiomatic: Lun told Guozhong: "Coinage requires skilled craftsmen; forcing farmers into the work wastes labor, yields little, and will breed resentment."

sentences.zh: 請厚懸市估價，募工曉者為之。

translations.literal: Please set a generous market price and recruit those skilled in the craft to do it.'
translations.idiomatic: Set a fair market wage and hire skilled workers instead."

sentences.zh: 」由是役使減少，而益鑄錢之數。

translations.literal: From this the corvée labor was reduced while the amount of coin cast increased.
translations.idiomatic: Corvée labor fell while coin output rose.

sentences.zh: 天寶末，宮內土木之功無虛日，內作人吏因緣為奸，倫乃躬親閱視，省費減倍。

translations.literal: At the end of the Tianbao era, within the palace there was no day without earthworks and carpentry; the clerks of inner works took advantage to commit fraud, and Lun personally inspected on site, reducing expenses by half.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Tianbao, palace construction never ceased; inner-work clerks profited by fraud until Lun inspected in person and cut costs by half.

sentences.zh: 改大理評事。

translations.literal: He was changed to Evaluator of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Evaluator in the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 會安祿山反，車駕幸蜀，拜倫監察御史、劍南節度行軍司馬，兼充置頓使判官，尋改屯田員外、兼侍御史。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled and the imperial carriage went to Shu, Lun was appointed Supervising Censor and Marching Sima of the Jiannan Military Commission, concurrently Acting Judge of the Encampment Commissioner, and soon changed to Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue and concurrently Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled and the court fled to Shu, Lun was made Supervising Censor and marching sima on the Jiannan staff, then Vice Director of Revenue and Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 時內官禁軍相次到蜀，所在侵暴，號為難理；

translations.literal: At that time inner eunuchs and the forbidden army arrived in Shu one after another; wherever they went they committed violence and were called hard to manage.
translations.idiomatic: Inner eunuchs and palace troops followed the court to Shu and plundered wherever they went.

sentences.zh: 倫清儉，率身以化之，蜀川鹹賴其理。

translations.literal: Lun was pure and frugal and led by personal example to transform them; the people of Shu all relied on his governance.
translations.idiomatic: Lun lived plainly and led by example until Sichuan was again governable.

sentences.zh: 竟遭中官毀譖，貶衡州司戶。

translations.literal: In the end he suffered slander by inner eunuchs and was demoted to Registrar of Sima in Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was eventually slandered by palace eunuchs and demoted to Registrar in Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 屬東都、河南並陷賊，漕運路絕，度支使第五琦薦倫有理能，拜商州刺史，充荊襄等道租庸使。

translations.literal: When both the Eastern Capital and Henan fell to the rebels and the grain transport routes were cut, Revenue Commissioner Di Wuqi recommended Lun as a man of governing ability and appointed him Prefect of Shangzhou, charged as Rent and Tax Commissioner for Jing-Xiang and other circuits.
translations.idiomatic: When Luoyang and Henan fell and transport routes were severed, Di Wuqi recommended Lun and appointed him Prefect of Shang, charged with collecting rent and tax on the Jing-Xiang routes.

sentences.zh: 會襄州裨將康楚元、張嘉延聚眾為叛，兇黨萬余人，自稱東楚義王。

translations.literal: At that time the assistant generals Kang Chuyuan and Zhang Jiayan of Xiangzhou gathered a crowd in rebellion; the violent faction numbered more than ten thousand and called itself the Eastern Chu Righteous King.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel leaders Kang Chuyuan and Zhang Jiayan of Xiangyang raised more than ten thousand men and styled themselves kings of Eastern Chu.

sentences.zh: 襄州刺史王政棄城遁走。

translations.literal: The Prefect of Xiangzhou Wang Zheng abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Wang Zheng of Xiangyang abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 嘉延又南襲破江陵，漢、沔饋運阻絕，朝廷旰食。

translations.literal: Jiayan again struck south and broke Jiangling; Han and Mian grain transport was blocked, and the court ate its meals late with anxiety.
translations.idiomatic: Jiayan then seized Jiangling to the south, cutting grain routes on the Han and Mian; the court faced famine with growing alarm.

sentences.zh: 倫乃調發兵甲駐鄧州界，兇黨有來降者，必厚加接待。

translations.literal: Lun then mobilized armor and troops and stationed them on the border of Dengzhou; when violent factions came to surrender he always received them generously.
translations.idiomatic: Lun mobilized troops to the Dengzhou frontier and treated every surrender generously.

sentences.zh: 數日後，楚元眾頗怠，倫進軍擊之。

translations.literal: After several days Chuyuan's followers grew quite slack, and Lun advanced the army to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: Within days Chuyuan's men grew lax, and Lun attacked.

sentences.zh: 生擒楚元以獻，余眾悉走散，收租庸錢物僅二百萬貫，並不失墜。

translations.literal: He captured Chuyuan alive and presented him; the rest of the crowd all scattered and fled, and the collected rent and tax goods of nearly two million strings were not lost.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Chuyuan alive, dispersed the rest, and recovered nearly two million strings in tax goods without loss.

sentences.zh: 荊、襄二州平。

translations.literal: Jing and Xiang two prefectures were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Jing and Xiang were pacified.

sentences.zh: 詔除崔光遠為襄州節度使，征倫為衛尉卿。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Cui Guangyuan Military Governor of Xiangzhou and summoned Lun as Director of the Court for Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: The court appointed Cui Guangyuan Military Governor of Xiang and recalled Lun as Director of the Court for Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 旬日，又以本官兼寧州刺史、招討處置等使，尋又兼隴州刺史。

translations.literal: Within ten days he was again given his regular office concurrently as Prefect of Ningzhou and Pacification and Disposition Commissioner, and soon also concurrently Prefect of Longzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ten days later he was also made Prefect of Ning and Pacification Commissioner, and soon Prefect of Long as well.

sentences.zh: 乾元三年，襄州大將張瑾殺節度使史翙作亂，乃以倫為襄州刺史、兼御史大夫、山南東道襄鄧等十州節度使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qianyuan the great general of Xiangzhou Zhang Jin killed Military Governor Shi Hui in revolt, and Lun was appointed Prefect of Xiangzhou, concurrently Censor-in-Chief and Military Governor of ten prefectures of Xiang and Deng in Shannan East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianyuan 3 (760) Zhang Jin killed Military Governor Shi Hui at Xiangyang; Lun was made Prefect of Xiang, Censor-in-Chief, and Military Governor of ten prefectures on the Shannan East route.

sentences.zh: 時李輔國秉權用事，節將除拜，皆出其門。

translations.literal: At that time Li Fuguo held power and managed affairs; military governors' appointments and dismissals all came from his gate.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fuguo then dominated appointments; every frontier commission passed through his favor.

sentences.zh: 倫既為朝廷公用，又不私謁輔國。

translations.literal: Lun was employed for public use by the court and did not pay private visits to Fuguo.
translations.idiomatic: Lun served the court's needs and refused private audiences with Fuguo.

sentences.zh: 倫受命未行，改秦州刺史、兼御史中丞、本州防禦使。

translations.literal: Lun had received the commission but had not yet departed when he was changed to Prefect of Qinzhou, concurrently Censor-in-Chief and Defense Commissioner of that prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Before Lun could depart he was transferred to Prefect of Qin, concurrently Censor-in-Chief and Defense Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時吐蕃、党項歲歲入寇，邊將奔命不暇。

translations.literal: At that time Tibetans and the Dangxiang tribes invaded every year, and frontier generals could not answer the emergency calls.
translations.idiomatic: Tibetans and Dangxiang raided yearly; frontier generals could not keep pace.

sentences.zh: 倫至秦州，屢與虜戰。

translations.literal: When Lun reached Qinzhou he fought the barbarians repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: At Qin Lun fought the invaders repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 兵寡無援，頻致敗衄，連貶巴州長史、思州務川縣尉。

translations.literal: His troops were few and without reinforcements; he frequently met defeat, was demoted in succession to Long Secretary of Bazhou and Warden of Wuchuan in Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Outnumbered and unsupported, he suffered repeated defeats and was demoted to secretary in Ba and warden in Wuchuan.

sentences.zh: 代宗即位，起為忠州刺史，歷臺、饒二州。

translations.literal: When Emperor Daizong took the throne, Lun was raised to Prefect of Zhongzhou and held in succession Taizhou and Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under Daizong he was restored to Prefect of Zhong and later governed Tai and Rao.

sentences.zh: 以中官呂太一於嶺南矯詔募兵為亂，乃以倫為韶州刺史、兼御史中丞、韶連柳三州都團練使。

translations.literal: Because the inner eunuch Lü Taiyi in Lingnan forged an edict to recruit troops in rebellion, Lun was appointed Prefect of Shaozhou, concurrently Censor-in-Chief and Commander-in-Chief of Sha, Lian, and Liu.
translations.idiomatic: When eunuch Lü Taiyi forged an edict to raise troops in Lingnan, Lun was made Prefect of Shao, Censor-in-Chief, and commander of Shao, Lian, and Liu.

sentences.zh: 竟遭太一用賂反間，貶信州司馬、虔州司戶、隋州司戶、隨州司馬。

translations.literal: In the end he suffered Taiyi's use of bribes and counterplots and was demoted in succession to Registrar of Sima in Xinzhou, Registrar in Qianzhou, Registrar in Suizhou, and Secretary in Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyi bribed and slandered him until he was demoted through a series of minor posts in Xin, Qian, Sui, and Sui again.

sentences.zh: 遇赦，旅寓於洪州十數年。

translations.literal: When an amnesty was granted, he lodged for more than ten years at Hongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After an amnesty he lived as a guest in Hong for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 德宗即位，選堪使絕域者，征倫拜太常少卿、兼御史中丞，持節充通和吐蕃使。

translations.literal: When Dezong took the throne, he selected men fit to serve in distant regions and summoned Lun, appointing him Vice Director of the Court for Imperial Sacrifices and concurrently Censor-in-Chief, bearing credentials as envoy for harmony with Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong sought men fit for distant missions and summoned Lun as Vice Director of Sacrifices and Censor-in-Chief, envoy to Tibet.

sentences.zh: 倫至蕃中，初宣諭皇恩，次述國威德遠振，蕃人大悅，贊普入獻方物。

translations.literal: When Lun reached the Tibetan lands he first proclaimed the imperial grace, then described how the state's authority and virtue extended far; the Tibetans were greatly pleased and the tsenpo came in to present local products.
translations.idiomatic: In Tibet he proclaimed imperial grace and the reach of Tang power; the Tibetans were pleased and the tsenpo sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 使還，遷太常卿、兼御史大夫，加銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: On his return he was promoted to Director of the Court for Imperial Sacrifices and concurrently Censor-in-Chief, with addition of Silver-Green Commissioner with the Splendid Purse.
translations.idiomatic: On return he became Director of Sacrifices and Censor-in-Chief with the Silver-Green rank.

sentences.zh: 再入吐蕃，奉使稱旨，西蕃敬服。

translations.literal: He entered Tibet a second time; his mission accorded with the imperial intent and the Western Tibetans respected and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: A second mission to Tibet likewise pleased the court and won Tibetan respect.

sentences.zh: 朝廷得失，數上疏言之。

translations.literal: The gains and losses of the court he memorialized on them in repeated memorials.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly memorialized the throne on the court's strengths and failings.

sentences.zh: 又為宰相盧杞所惡，改太子少保，累加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: He was again hated by Chief Minister Lu Qi and was changed to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, with cumulative addition of Grand Master of the Palace with the Splendid Purse bearing the Golden Seal.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Lu Qi disliked him and moved him to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, later adding Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 涇師之亂，駕幸奉天。

translations.literal: When the Jingzhou troops rebelled, the imperial carriage went to Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingzhou mutiny the emperor fled to Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 及盧杞、白誌貞、趙贊等貶官，關播罷相為刑部尚書，倫於朝堂嗚咽而言曰：「宰相不能弼諧啟沃，使天下一至於此。

translations.literal: When Lu Qi, Bai Zhizhen, Zhao Zan, and others were demoted and Guan Bo was removed from the chief ministership to become Minister of Justice, Lun wept aloud in the court hall, saying: 'The chief ministers could not assist and harmonize or offer counsel and nourishment, and let the realm come to this.'
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Qi and others were demoted and Guan Bo was reduced to Minister of Justice, Lun wept in court: "The chief ministers failed to counsel the throne and brought the empire to this pass."

sentences.zh: 仍為尚書，天下何由致理？

translations.literal: Yet he remains Minister of Revenue—how can the realm attain good order?'
translations.idiomatic: Yet he remains Minister of Revenue—how can the realm be governed?"

sentences.zh: 」聞者敬憚之。

translations.literal: Those who heard were respectful and in awe.
translations.idiomatic: Listeners were struck with respect and dread.

sentences.zh: 從駕梁州，還京，又欲擢用盧杞為饒州刺史。

translations.literal: Following the imperial carriage to Liangzhou and returning to the capital, the court again wished to promote Lu Qi as Prefect of Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: After accompanying the court to Liang and back, the throne again wished to appoint Lu Qi Prefect of Rao.

sentences.zh: 倫又上表切言不可，深為忠正之士所稱嘆。

translations.literal: Lun again submitted a memorial urgently stating it could not be done, and was deeply praised by upright loyal men.
translations.idiomatic: Lun memorialized urgently against it and won praise from upright officials.

sentences.zh: 以年逾七十，表請休官，改太子少師致仕，封郢國公。

translations.literal: Because he passed seventy years of age he submitted a memorial requesting retirement, was changed to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent with retirement, and enfeoffed as Duke of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: At over seventy he sought retirement, was made Junior Tutor emeritus, and enfeoffed Duke of Ying.

sentences.zh: 時李楚琳以僕射兼衛尉卿，李忠誠以尚書兼少府監，倫上言曰：「楚琳兇逆，忠誠蕃戎醜類，不合廁列清班。

translations.literal: At that time Li Chulin held the post of Vice Director while also Director of the Court for Imperial Sacrifices, and Li Zhongcheng held the post of Minister while also Vice Director of the Palace Domestic Service; Lun submitted a memorial saying: 'Chulin is violent and rebellious, Zhongcheng a vile sort from the western barbarians—they should not stand in the pure ranks.'
translations.idiomatic: When Li Chulin and Li Zhongcheng held incompatible dual posts, Lun protested that a rebel and a barbarian favorite did not belong in court rank.

sentences.zh: 」又表請置義倉以防水旱，擇賢良任之左右。

translations.literal: He also memorialized requesting establishment of charity granaries to guard against flood and drought, and selection of worthy and good men to serve at the ruler's side.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged charity granaries against flood and drought and the appointment of worthy counselors.

sentences.zh: 又言吐蕃必無信約，專須防備，不可輕易。

translations.literal: He also said Tibet would surely not keep faith and must be guarded against and could not be treated lightly.
translations.idiomatic: He warned that Tibet would break faith and must never be trusted lightly.

sentences.zh: 上每善遇之。

translations.literal: The emperor always treated him kindly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor always received him graciously.

sentences.zh: 倫居家孝友，撫弟侄以慈愛稱。

translations.literal: Lun at home was filial and friendly and raised younger brothers and nephews with a reputation for loving kindness.
translations.idiomatic: At home Lun was famed for filial piety and kindness to younger kin.

sentences.zh: 貞元十四年十二月卒，時年八十三，贈揚州都督。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the fourteenth year of Zhenyuan he died, aged eighty-three, and was posthumously enfeoffed as Area Commander of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twelfth month of Zhenyuan 14 (798), aged eighty-three, and was posthumously made Area Commander of Yang.

sentences.zh: 賈耽，字敦詩，滄州南皮人。

translations.literal: Jia Dan, styled Dunshi, was a man of Nanpi in Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Dan (styled Dunshi) came from Nanpi in Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 以兩經登第，調授貝州臨清縣尉。

translations.literal: He passed the examinations in both classics, was appointed and transferred as Warden of Linqing in Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He passed both classics examinations and was appointed magistrate of Linqing in Bei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 上疏論時政，授絳州正平尉。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial discussing the politics of the time and was appointed Warden of Zhengping in Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on current affairs and was made magistrate of Zhengping in Jiang.

sentences.zh: 從事河東，檢校膳部員外郎、太原少尹、北都副留守。

translations.literal: He served on the staff in Hedong, was appointed Acting Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites, Junior Vice Director of Taiyuan, and Deputy Military Governor of the Northern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the Hedong staff he became Acting Vice Director of Rites, Junior Vice Director of Taiyuan, and Deputy Military Governor of the Northern Capital.

sentences.zh: 又檢校禮部郎中、節度副使，改汾州刺史。

translations.literal: He was again Acting Director of the Ministry of Rites and Deputy Military Commissioner, and was changed to Prefect of Fenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Acting Director of Rites and deputy commissioner, then Prefect of Fen.

sentences.zh: 在郡七年，政績茂異。

translations.literal: In the prefecture seven years, his administrative achievements were outstandingly abundant.
translations.idiomatic: For seven years in Fen his achievements were outstanding.

sentences.zh: 入為鴻臚卿，時左右威遠營隸鴻臚，耽仍領其使。

translations.literal: He entered the court as Director of the Court for Diplomatic Relations; at that time the Left and Right Weiyuan Camps were subordinate to that office, and Dan still headed their commission.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as Director of Diplomatic Relations, still overseeing the Weiyuan guard camps attached to that office.

sentences.zh: 大歷十四年十一月，檢校左散騎常侍、兼梁州刺史、御史大夫、山南西道節度使。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the fourteenth year of Dali he was appointed Acting Left Regular Attendant, concurrently Prefect of Liangzhou, Censor-in-Chief, and Military Governor of Shannan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In Dali 14 (779) he was made Acting Left Regular Attendant, Prefect of Liang, Censor-in-Chief, and Military Governor of Shannan West.

sentences.zh: 建中三年十一月，檢校工部尚書、兼御史大夫、山南東道節度使。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the third year of Jianzhong he was appointed Acting Minister of Works, concurrently Censor-in-Chief and Military Governor of Shannan East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianzhong 3 (782) he became Acting Minister of Works, Censor-in-Chief, and Military Governor of Shannan East.

sentences.zh: 德宗移幸梁州。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong moved the capital to Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong moved the court to Liang.

sentences.zh: 興元元年二月，耽使行軍司馬樊澤奏事於行在，澤既復命，方大宴諸將，有急牒至，言澤代耽為節度使，而召耽為工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Xingyuan Dan's Marching Sima Fan Ze reported affairs at the mobile court; Ze had just returned with his report when a urgent dispatch arrived saying Ze had replaced Dan as military governor and Dan was summoned as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In Xingyuan 1 (784) his marching sima Fan Ze reported at the mobile court; while Dan feasted his generals, an urgent dispatch arrived naming Ze his replacement and summoning Dan as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 耽得牒內懷中，宴飲不改容。

translations.literal: Dan received the dispatch and kept it inside his robe; the feast and drinking did not change his expression.
translations.idiomatic: Dan hid the dispatch in his robe and continued the feast without changing expression.

sentences.zh: 及散，召樊澤，以詔授之曰：「詔以行軍為節度使，耽今即上路。

translations.literal: When the feast ended he summoned Fan Ze and gave him the edict, saying: 'The edict makes the marching commander military governor; Dan now at once takes the road.'
translations.idiomatic: When the feast ended he handed Ze the edict: "You are military governor; I leave at once."

sentences.zh: 」因告將吏使謁澤。

translations.literal: He then told the generals and clerks to call on Ze.
translations.idiomatic: He told his officers to pay court to Ze.

sentences.zh: 牙將張獻甫曰：「天子巡幸山南，尚書使行軍奉表起居，而行軍敢自圖節鉞，潛奪尚書土地，此可謂事人不忠。

translations.literal: The牙將 Zhang Xianfu said: 'The Son of Heaven is touring Shannan; the Minister sent the Marching Commander to present a memorial of inquiry, yet the Marching Commander dared to plot for the commander's seal himself and secretly seize the Minister's territory—this may be called serving others without loyalty.'
translations.idiomatic: General Zhang Xianfu protested: "The emperor is on campaign and the Minister sent Ze to court—yet Ze stole his command. That is disloyalty."

sentences.zh: 軍中皆不伏，請殺樊澤。

translations.literal: The army was all discontented and asked to kill Fan Ze.
translations.idiomatic: The troops demanded Ze's death.

sentences.zh: 」耽曰：「公是何言歟！

translations.literal: Dan said: 'Sir, what words are these!'
translations.idiomatic: Dan said: "What talk is this!"

sentences.zh: 天子有命，即為節度使矣。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven has a command—he is already military governor.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven has spoken—Ze is governor.

sentences.zh: 耽今赴行在，便與公偕行。

translations.literal: Dan now goes to the mobile court and will travel with you together.'
translations.idiomatic: I go to the emperor now and will travel with you."

sentences.zh: 」即日離鎮，以獻甫自隨，軍中乃安。

translations.literal: That same day he left his post, taking Xianfu with him, and the army was then at peace.
translations.idiomatic: That day he departed with Xianfu, and the army accepted the change.

sentences.zh: 尋以本官為東都留守、東畿汝南防禦使。

translations.literal: Soon with his regular office he became Military Governor of the Eastern Capital and Defense Commissioner of the Eastern Metropolitan Region and Runan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became Military Governor of the Eastern Capital and Defense Commissioner of the eastern metropolitan region.

sentences.zh: 貞元二年，改檢校右僕射、兼滑州刺史、義成軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenyuan he was changed to Acting Right Vice Director, concurrently Prefect of Huazhou and Military Governor of the Yicheng Army.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 2 (786) he became Acting Right Vice Director, Prefect of Hua, and Military Governor of Yicheng.

sentences.zh: 是時淄青節度使李納雖去偽王號，外奉朝旨，而心常蓄並吞之謀。

translations.literal: At that time the Military Governor of Ziqing Li Na though he had removed the false royal title outwardly followed court instructions, yet in his heart he constantly harbored schemes of swallowing and merging.
translations.idiomatic: Li Na of Ziqing had dropped his rebel title but still plotted expansion.

sentences.zh: 納兵士數千人自行營歸，路由滑州，大將請城外館之。

translations.literal: Several thousand of Na's soldiers returning from their own camps passed by Huazhou on the route; the great general asked to lodge them outside the city.
translations.idiomatic: Thousands of Li Na's men marching home asked to camp outside Hua.

sentences.zh: 耽曰：「與人鄰道，奈何野處其兵？

translations.literal: Dan said: 'We are neighbors on the same road—how can we let their troops lodge in the wild?'
translations.idiomatic: Dan said: "We are neighbors—how can I quarter your men in the open?"

sentences.zh: 」命館之城內，淄青將士皆心服之。

translations.literal: He ordered them lodged within the city, and the Ziqing officers and soldiers all submitted in heart.
translations.idiomatic: He housed them inside the walls, and Ziqing troops admired his magnanimity.

sentences.zh: 耽善射好獵，每出畋不過百騎，往往獵於李納之境。

translations.literal: Dan was skilled at archery and loved the hunt; whenever he went out hunting it was never more than a hundred horsemen, and he often hunted within Li Na's borders.
translations.idiomatic: Dan was an archer and hunter who never took more than a hundred riders, often hunting in Li Na's territory.

sentences.zh: 納聞之，大喜，心畏其度量，不敢異圖。

translations.literal: When Na heard of it he was greatly pleased and in heart feared Dan's magnanimity, not daring other designs.
translations.idiomatic: Li Na was pleased yet intimidated by Dan's confidence and dared no fresh intrigue.

sentences.zh: 九年，征為右僕射、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was summoned as Right Vice Director and Fellow of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was summoned as Right Vice Director and Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 耽好地理學，凡四夷之使及使四夷還者，必與之從容，訊其山川土地之終始。

translations.literal: Dan loved the study of geography; whenever envoys from the four barbarians or those returning from missions to the four barbarians came, he always conversed with them at leisure, inquiring into the beginning and end of their mountains, rivers, and lands.
translations.idiomatic: Dan loved geography and questioned every envoy from or to the frontier about the lands they had seen.

sentences.zh: 是以九州之夷險，百蠻之土俗，區分指畫，備究源流。

translations.literal: Therefore the ruggedness and ease of the nine provinces, the customs of the hundred barbarians, he distinguished and mapped, fully investigating origins and currents.
translations.idiomatic: Thus he charted the terrain of the nine provinces and the customs of myriad peoples, tracing every source and route.

sentences.zh: 自吐蕃陷隴右積年，國家守於內地，舊時鎮戍，不可復知。

translations.literal: Since Tibet occupied Longyou for successive years, the state guarded the inner lands, and the old garrison posts could no longer be known.
translations.idiomatic: After Tibet held Longyou for years, the court retreated inland and lost track of former garrison posts.

sentences.zh: 耽乃畫隴右、山南圖，兼黃河經界遠近，聚其說為書十卷，表獻曰：

translations.literal: Dan then drew maps of Longyou and Shannan, together with the Yellow River's boundaries near and far, gathered the accounts into ten scrolls of writing, and submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: He drew maps of Longyou and Shannan with the Yellow River's course, compiled ten scrolls of notes, and memorialized:

sentences.zh: 臣聞楚左史倚相能讀《九丘》，晉司空裴秀創為六體；

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that the Left Historiographer of Chu, Yi Xiang, could read the 'Nine Mounds,' and the Minister of Works of Jin, Pei Xiu, created the six forms.
translations.idiomatic: As Yi Xiang of Chu read the Nine Mounds and Pei Xiu of Jin devised the six cartographic forms,

sentences.zh: 《九丘》乃成賦之古經，六體則為圖之新意。

translations.literal: The 'Nine Mounds' is the ancient classic on which Cheng Fu was based; the six forms are the new idea in maps.
translations.idiomatic: the Nine Mounds was the ancient classic of realms, and the six forms a new cartographic method.

sentences.zh: 臣雖愚昧，夙嘗師範，累蒙拔擢，遂忝臺司。

translations.literal: Your servant, though foolish and dull, has long had teachers and models, and repeatedly received promotion, thus presumptuously bearing a seat in the council.
translations.idiomatic: Though unlearned, I have long studied under masters and, promoted repeatedly, now hold a seat at court.

sentences.zh: 雖歷踐職任，誠多曠闕，而率土山川，不忘寤寐。

translations.literal: Though in successive offices my fulfillment has had many gaps, the mountains and rivers of the realm I have not forgotten even in sleep.
translations.idiomatic: Though I have often fallen short in office, I have never ceased to study the empire's mountains and rivers.

sentences.zh: 其大圖外薄四海，內別九州，必藉精詳，乃可摹寫，見更纘集，續冀畢功。

translations.literal: The great map thinly covers the four seas and within distinguishes the nine provinces; it must rely on minute detail before it can be copied; I see it is being further compiled and continue to hope for completion.
translations.idiomatic: A great map embracing the four seas and marking the nine provinces requires exact detail; I am compiling further and hope soon to finish.

sentences.zh: 然而隴右一隅，久淪蕃寇，職方失其圖記，境土難以區分。

translations.literal: Yet the corner of Longyou has long fallen to the barbarian raiders; the Bureau of Duty has lost its maps and records, and the borderlands are hard to distinguish.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Longyou has long been lost to Tibet; official maps are gone and borders hard to trace.

sentences.zh: 輒扣課虛微，采掇輿議，畫《關中隴右及山南九州等圖》一軸。

translations.literal: Your servant has hastily sought out the slight and subtle, gathered popular opinion, and drawn one scroll of the 'Map of Guanzhong, Longyou, and the Nine Provinces of Shannan and Others.'
translations.idiomatic: I have therefore gathered what reports remain and drawn a map of Guanzhong, Longyou, and Shannan.

sentences.zh: 伏以洮、湟舊墟，連接監牧；

translations.literal: I humbly consider that the old sites of Tao and Huang connect with the border pastures.
translations.idiomatic: The Tao and Huang region links to frontier pastures;

sentences.zh: 甘、涼右地，控帶朔陲。

translations.literal: The right lands of Gan and Liang control the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Gan and Liang guard the northern marches.

sentences.zh: 岐路之偵候交通，軍鎮之備禦沖要，莫不匠意就實，依稀像真。

translations.literal: Crossroads for scouts and communications, military posts for defense at strategic points—all were fashioned with intent toward reality, roughly like the truth.
translations.idiomatic: Roads, scouts, garrisons, and passes are drawn as close to fact as I could make them.

sentences.zh: 如聖恩遣將護邊，新書授律，則靈、慶之設險在目，原、會之封略可知。

translations.literal: If sacred grace sends generals to guard the border and new writings grant military law, then the defenses of Ling and Qing would be before the eyes, and the sealed borders of Yuan and Hui would be knowable.
translations.idiomatic: Should Your Majesty send generals to the frontier, the terrain of Ling, Qing, Yuan, and Hui will lie plain before them.

sentences.zh: 諸州諸軍，須論里數人額；

translations.literal: The various prefectures and armies must discuss li distances and head counts.
translations.idiomatic: Every prefecture and army is marked with distances and troop numbers;

sentences.zh: 諸山諸水，須言首尾源流。

translations.literal: The various mountains and waters must state headwaters, tails, origins, and currents.
translations.idiomatic: every mountain and river with its source and course.

sentences.zh: 圖上不可備書，憑據必資記註，謹撰《別錄》六卷。

translations.literal: On the map one cannot write everything in full; reliance must be on written notes, and your servant respectfully compiled six scrolls of 'Separate Records.'
translations.idiomatic: The map cannot hold every note; I submit six scrolls of Separate Records.

sentences.zh: 又黃河為四瀆之宗，西戎乃群羌之帥，臣並研尋史牒，翦棄浮詞，罄所聞知，編為四卷，通錄都成十卷。

translations.literal: Also the Yellow River is the head of the four great rivers, and the Western Rong are leaders of the many Qiang tribes; your servant researched historical records, cut away floating words, exhausted what was heard and known, compiled four scrolls, and in total the collection makes ten scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: I also compiled four scrolls on the Yellow River and the western tribes, making ten scrolls in all.

sentences.zh: 文義鄙樸，伏增慚悚。

translations.literal: The literary meaning is crude and plain; I humbly increase shame and fear.
translations.idiomatic: The writing is plain; I offer it with deep humility.

sentences.zh: 德宗覽之稱善，賜廄馬一匹、銀采百匹、銀瓶盤各一。

translations.literal: Dezong perused it and praised it, bestowing one stable horse, a hundred bolts of colored silk, and one each of silver bottle and tray.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong praised it and granted a horse, a hundred bolts of silk, and silver vessels.

sentences.zh: 至十七年，又撰成《海內華夷圖》及《古今郡國縣道四夷述》四十卷，表獻之，曰：

translations.literal: By the seventeenth year he again completed the 'Map of Chinese and Barbarians Within the Seas' and the 'Account of Ancient and Modern Commanderies, Counties, Roads, and the Four Barbarians' in forty scrolls, and submitted them with a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: In his seventeenth year he finished the great Map of Chinese and Barbarians Within the Seas and a forty-scroll geographical treatise, memorializing:

sentences.zh: 臣聞地以博厚載物，萬國棋布；

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that the earth by vast thickness bears the myriad things; the ten thousand states are laid out like chess pieces.
translations.idiomatic: The earth bears all things; the myriad states lie like pieces on a board.

sentences.zh: 海以委輸環外，百蠻繡錯。

translations.literal: The sea by pouring transport encircles the outer realm; the hundred barbarians are embroidered and interlaced.
translations.idiomatic: The seas encircle the world; barbarian lands weave among them.

sentences.zh: 中夏則五服、九州，殊俗則七戎、六狄，普天之下，莫非王臣。

translations.literal: Within China are the five domains and nine provinces; among foreign customs are the seven Rong and six Di; under all heaven there are none who are not the king's subjects.
translations.idiomatic: China has its nine provinces; beyond are the Rong and Di—yet all are the Son of Heaven's subjects.

sentences.zh: 昔毋丘出師，東銘不耐；

translations.literal: In former times Wuqiu went out with the army and eastward inscribed Bu Nai.
translations.idiomatic: Wuqiu marched east and inscribed his victory;

sentences.zh: 甘英奉使，西抵條支；

translations.literal: Gan Ying received a mission and westward reached Tiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Ying went west to Tiaozhi;

sentences.zh: 奄蔡乃大澤無涯，罽賓則懸度作險。

translations.literal: Yan Cai was a great marsh without bound; Ji Bin hung precarious on a rope bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Cai was an endless marsh; Ji Bin a land of rope bridges.

sentences.zh: 或道理回遠，或名號改移，古來通儒，罕遍詳究。

translations.literal: Some roads and principles turned far, some names and titles changed and shifted; ancient comprehensive scholars rarely fully investigated in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Routes were remote and names changed; few scholars of old mastered it all.

sentences.zh: 臣弱冠之歲，好聞方言，筮仕之辰，註意地理，究觀研考，垂三十年。

translations.literal: In the years of your servant's weak cap he loved to hear dialects; in the day of taking office he fixed attention on geography, investigating and examining for nearly thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: From youth I loved foreign tongues; since entering office I have studied geography for nearly thirty years.

sentences.zh: 絕域之比鄰，異蕃之習俗，梯山獻琛之路，乘舶來朝之人，鹹究竟其源流，訪求其居處。

translations.literal: Neighboring lands of the farthest regions, customs of alien tribes, roads over mountains by which tribute was offered, men who came by ship in court audience—all origins and currents were ultimately traced, dwellings and locations sought out.
translations.idiomatic: I traced the routes of tribute missions and foreign envoys to their sources and homes.

sentences.zh: 阛阓之行賈，戎貊之遺老，莫不聽其言而掇其要。

translations.literal: Market-street traveling merchants and surviving elders of the Rong and Mo—all were heard and their essentials gathered.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants and frontier elders alike were questioned and their accounts recorded.

sentences.zh: 閭閻之瑣語，風謠之小說，亦收其是而芟其偽。

translations.literal: Neighborhood trivial talk and popular minor tales—also what was right was received and what was false was cut away.
translations.idiomatic: Popular tales were accepted when true and discarded when false.

sentences.zh: 然殷、周以降，封略益明，承歷數者八家，渾區宇者五姓，聲教所及，惟唐為大。

translations.literal: Yet from Yin and Zhou downward the sealed boundaries grew clearer; eight houses bore the succession of numbers, five surnames unified the realm's quarters; where sound and teaching reached, only Tang was greatest.
