translations.idiomatic: Since Yin and Zhou borders grew clearer; through eight dynasties and five ruling houses, none spread civilization like Tang.

sentences.zh: 秦皇罷侯置守，長城起於臨洮；

translations.literal: The First Emperor of Qin abolished the feudal lords and set defenders; the Long Wall rose from Lintao.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Shihuang abolished feudal lords and built the Long Wall from Lintao.

sentences.zh: 孝武卻地開邊，障塞限於雞鹿；

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Han pushed back territory and opened the frontier; barriers and passes were limited at Jilu.
translations.idiomatic: Han Wudi pushed the frontier to Jilu.

sentences.zh: 東漢則哀牢請吏；

translations.literal: Eastern Han then had Aila request officials.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Han received Aila as a subject;

sentences.zh: 西晉則裨離結轍；

translations.literal: Western Jin then had Piluo join in file.
translations.idiomatic: Western Jin saw Piluo arrive in procession.

sentences.zh: 隋室列四郡於卑和海西，創三州於扶南江北，遼陽失律，因而棄之。

translations.literal: The Sui house set four commanderies west of the Pei and Hai seas, created three prefectures north of the Fu Nan River; Liaoyang lost discipline and was therefore abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Sui founded commanderies on the western sea; Liaoyang was later abandoned.

sentences.zh: 高祖神堯皇帝誕膺天命，奄有四方。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor, the Divine Yao Emperor, received Heaven's mandate and suddenly possessed the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu received Heaven's mandate and seized the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 太宗繼明重熙，柔遠能邇，逾大磧通道，北至仙娥，於骨利幹置玄闕州。

translations.literal: Taizong continued bright repeated glory, was gentle to the distant and able toward the near; crossed the great desert to open the road, north to Xian'e, and at Guligan set the Xuanque Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong pacified the far reaches, opened roads across the desert, and founded Xuanque Prefecture in the north.

sentences.zh: 高宗嗣守丕績，克廣前烈，遣單車賫詔，西越蔥山，於波刺斯立疾陵府。

translations.literal: Gaozong continued guarding the great enterprise, expanded the former achievements, sent a single carriage bearing an edict west beyond Cong Mountain, and at Bosi established the Jiling Protectorate.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong extended the realm, sent envoys beyond Cong Mountain, and founded Jiling in Persia.

sentences.zh: 中宗復配天之業，不失舊物。

translations.literal: Zhongzong restored the enterprise matching Heaven and did not lose the old possessions.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong restored the imperial patrimony.

sentences.zh: 睿宗含先天之量，惟新永圖。

translations.literal: Ruizong contained the measure of prior Heaven and renewed the eternal plan.
translations.idiomatic: Ruizong renewed the eternal design of rule.

sentences.zh: 玄宗以大孝清內，以無為理外，大宛驥錄，歲充內廄，與貳師之窮兵黷武，豈同年哉！

translations.literal: Xuanzong by great filial piety cleared the inner realm, by non-action governed the outer; great Yuan horses were recorded yearly to fill the inner stables—with the exhausted soldiers and martial excess of the Second Master, how could they be the same year!
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong ruled inward by filial piety and outward by non-action; his horse tribute was not Wudi's ruinous warfare.

sentences.zh: 肅宗掃平氛昆，潤澤生人。

translations.literal: Suzong swept away turbid vapors and moistened living men.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong swept away rebellion and nourished the people.

sentences.zh: 代宗刬除殘孽，彜倫攸敘。

translations.literal: Daizong cut away the remnant evil and constant norms were set in order.
translations.idiomatic: Daizong destroyed the rebel remnant and restored order.

sentences.zh: 伏惟皇帝陛下，以上聖之姿，當太平之運，敦信明義，履信包元，惠養黎蒸，懷柔遐裔。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that Your Majesty, with the posture of the highest sage, meets the fortune of great peace, honors faith and clarifies righteousness, treads faith and embraces the origin, kindly nurtures the black-headed people, and cherishes and softens the distant borderlands.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, supreme sage in an age of peace, nurtures the people and cherishes distant realms.

sentences.zh: 故瀘南貢麗水之金，漠北獻余吾之馬，玄化洋溢，率士沾濡。

translations.literal: Therefore Lunan presented gold of the Lishui, the desert north presented horses of Yuyu; mysterious transformation overflowed and all within the realm were moistened.
translations.idiomatic: Lishui gold and northern horses flow in tribute; your grace reaches all under heaven.

sentences.zh: 臣幼切磋於師友，長趨侍於軒墀，自揣孱愚，叨榮非據，鴻私莫答，夙夜兢惶。

translations.literal: Your servant in youth polished himself with teachers and friends, in maturity hastened to attend the palace threshold; measuring himself foolish and dull, he presumptuously bore unfitting honor; the great private kindness cannot be answered, morning and night fearful and cautious.
translations.idiomatic: I have long served at court, unworthy of my post, and tremble before your grace.

sentences.zh: 去興元元年，伏奉進止，令臣修撰國圖，旋即充使魏州、汴州，出鎮東洛、東都，間以眾務，不遂專門，績用尚虧，憂愧彌切。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xingyuan I humbly received orders to have your servant compile the national maps; soon I was sent as envoy to Weizhou and Bianzhou and went out to govern the eastern capital; amid many duties I could not specialize, achievement still lacking, worry and shame ever keener.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered in Xingyuan 1 to compile national maps, I was diverted by missions and governorships and could not finish—my shame is keen.

sentences.zh: 近乃力竭衰病，思殫所聞見，叢於丹青。

translations.literal: Recently my strength was exhausted by decline and illness, and I thought to exhaust what I have heard and seen, gathering it in ink and color.
translations.idiomatic: Now, worn by age and illness, I have set down all I know in ink.

sentences.zh: 謹令工人畫《海內華夷圖》一軸，廣三丈，從三丈三尺，率以一寸折成百里。

translations.literal: Respectfully ordering craftsmen to paint one scroll of the 'Map of Chinese and Barbarians Within the Seas,' three zhang wide and three zhang three chi from top to bottom, at the rate of one cun folding into a hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: I present a map three zhang wide, scaled so one inch equals a hundred li.

sentences.zh: 別章甫左衽，奠高山大川。

translations.literal: Separately marking left-collared barbarians, setting out high mountains and great rivers.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarian lands are marked apart; mountains and rivers are shown in full.

sentences.zh: 縮四極於纖縞，分百郡於作繢。

translations.literal: Contracting the four extremities onto fine silk, dividing the hundred commanderies into painted work.
translations.idiomatic: The four quarters are drawn on silk; the hundred commanderies painted in.

sentences.zh: 宇宙雖廣，舒之不盈庭；

translations.literal: Though the cosmos is vast, spread out it does not fill the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Though the world is vast, unfolded it fits within a hall.

sentences.zh: 舟車所通，覽之鹹在目。

translations.literal: Where boat and cart can reach, gazing upon it all lies before the eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Every place reached by road or river lies before the eye.

sentences.zh: 並撰《古今郡國縣道四夷述》四十卷，中國以《禹貢》為首，外夷以《班史》發源；

translations.literal: Also compiled the 'Account of Ancient and Modern Commanderies, Counties, Roads, and the Four Barbarians' in forty scrolls; within China the 'Tribute of Yu' is taken as head, among outer barbarians the 'Han History' as source.
translations.idiomatic: With it I submit a forty-scroll treatise, China following the Tribute of Yu, foreign lands the Han History.

sentences.zh: 郡縣紀其增減，蕃落敘其衰盛。

translations.literal: Commanderies and counties record their increase and decrease; barbarian settlements narrate their decline and flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: Commanderies record their changes; barbarian tribes their rise and fall.

sentences.zh: 前地理書以黔州屬酉陽，今則改入巴郡；

translations.literal: Former geographical books placed Qianzhou in Youyang; now it is changed to enter Bazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Old geographies placed Qian in Youyang; I correct it to Ba.

sentences.zh: 前西戎誌以安國為安息，今則改入康居。

translations.literal: The former Western Rong Account took An Kingdom as Parthia; now it is changed to enter Kangju.
translations.idiomatic: Old western accounts mistook An for Parthia; I place it in Kangju.

sentences.zh: 凡諸疏舛，悉從厘正。

translations.literal: Wherever there were omissions and errors, all followed careful correction.
translations.idiomatic: Every error I found has been corrected.

sentences.zh: 隴西、十地，播棄於永初之中；

translations.literal: Longxi and the ten regions were cast away in the middle of Yongchu.
translations.idiomatic: Longxi and ten regions were lost in the Yongchu era;

sentences.zh: 遼東、樂浪，陷屈於建安之際。

translations.literal: Liaodong and Lelang sank into submission in the Jian'an period.
translations.idiomatic: Liaodong and Lelang fell in Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 曹公棄陘北，晉氏遷江南，緣邊累經侵盜，故墟日致堙毀。

translations.literal: Cao Gong abandoned north of the passes; the Jin house moved south of the river; the borderlands repeatedly suffered invasion and plunder, and old sites daily fell to ruin and destruction.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao lost the north, Jin retreated south, and borderlands crumbled.

sentences.zh: 舊史撰錄，十得二三，今書搜補，所獲太半。

translations.literal: Old histories in writing obtained two or three out of ten; the present book in search and supplement obtained more than half.
translations.idiomatic: Old records preserved scarcely a fifth; my book recovers more than half.

sentences.zh: 《周禮職方》，以淄、時為幽州之浸，以華山為荊河之鎮，既有乖於《禹貢》，又不出於淹中，多聞闕疑，詎敢編次。

translations.literal: The 'Zhou Offices' Directorate of Duty took Zi and Shi as the marshes of Youzhou, took Mount Hua as the anchor of Jing and He—already at odds with the 'Tribute of Yu' and also not coming forth from Yanzhong; hearing much and doubting, how dare one compile and arrange?
translations.idiomatic: Where the Zhou Offices conflict with the Tribute of Yu I have not dared to force a system.

sentences.zh: 其古郡國題以墨，今州縣題以硃，今古殊文，執習簡易。

translations.literal: Ancient commanderies and states are titled in ink; present prefectures and counties in cinnabar; ancient and present different scripts, holding and practicing simple and easy.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient names appear in black, modern in red, for ease of reading.

sentences.zh: 臣學謝小成，才非博物。

translations.literal: Your servant's learning stops at small achievement; talent is not that of broad investigation.
translations.idiomatic: My learning is slight, my talent not that of a polymath.

sentences.zh: 伏波之聚米，開示眾軍；

translations.literal: Fubo gathering rice showed the many armies.
translations.idiomatic: As Fubo modeled grain to brief his troops,

sentences.zh: 酂侯之圖書，方知厄塞。

translations.literal: The Marquis of Zan's maps and writings then made known strategic passes.
translations.idiomatic: and the Marquis of Zan used maps to reveal the passes,

sentences.zh: 企慕前哲，嘗所寄心，輒罄庸陋，多慚紕繆。

translations.literal: Looking up to former sages, I have always entrusted my heart; now exhausting mediocrity and ugliness, I am much ashamed of errors.
translations.idiomatic: so I have tried to follow their example, though my work is full of flaws.

sentences.zh: 優詔答之，賜錦彩二百匹、袍段六、錦帳二、銀瓶盤各一、銀榼二、馬一匹，進封魏國公。

translations.literal: An excellent edict answered him, bestowing two hundred bolts of brocade silk, six robes, two brocade curtains, one each of silver bottle and tray, two silver flasks, and one horse, with advancement enfeoffed as Duke of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor answered graciously with silk, robes, vessels, a horse, and enfeoffed him Duke of Wei.

sentences.zh: 順宗即位，檢校司空，守左僕射，知政事如故。

translations.literal: When Shunzong took the throne, Dan was appointed Acting Minister of Works, holding Left Vice Director and managing government affairs as before.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shunzong he was Acting Minister of Works, holding Left Vice Director and continuing in government.

sentences.zh: 時王叔文用事，政出群小，耽惡其亂政，屢移病乞骸，不許。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Shuwen held power; government came from a clique of petty men; Dan hated their disorder in government and several times moved illness to beg his bones, but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shuwen then dominated the court; Dan detested the disorder and repeatedly sought retirement in vain.

sentences.zh: 耽性長者，不喜臧否人物。

translations.literal: Dan's nature was that of an elder; he did not like to judge people's faults and merits.
translations.idiomatic: Dan was by nature forbearing and seldom judged others.

sentences.zh: 自居相位，凡十三年，雖不能以安危大計啟沃於人主，而常以檢身厲行以律人。

translations.literal: From the time he held the chief minister's seat for thirteen years, though he could not with great plans of safety and peril offer counsel and nourishment to the sovereign, he always used examining himself and strict conduct to regulate others.
translations.idiomatic: For thirteen years as chief minister he could not always counsel the throne on grand strategy, yet he disciplined himself and set an example for others.

sentences.zh: 每自朝歸第，接對賓客，終日無倦。

translations.literal: Whenever he returned from court to his residence, receiving and answering guests, there was no weariness all day.
translations.idiomatic: Returning home from court he received guests tirelessly all day.

sentences.zh: 至於家人近習，未嘗見其喜慍之色，古之淳德君子，何以加焉！

translations.literal: As for family and close attendants, they never saw the color of his joy or anger; how could the pure virtue gentlemen of antiquity be added to this!
translations.idiomatic: Even servants never saw him show anger—surpassing the gentle sages of old.

sentences.zh: 永貞元年十月卒，時年七十六。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the first year of Yongzhen he died, aged seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the tenth month of Yongzhen 1 (805), aged seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 廢朝四日，冊贈太傅，謚曰元靖。

translations.literal: Court was suspended four days; he was enfeoffed posthumously as Grand Tutor with posthumous title Yuanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Court mourned four days; he was posthumously Grand Tutor with the title Yuanjing.

sentences.zh: 姜公輔

translations.literal: Jiang Gongfu
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Gongfu

sentences.zh: 姜公輔，不知何許人。

translations.literal: Jiang Gongfu—no one knows from what place he came.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Gongfu—his native place is unknown.

sentences.zh: 登進士第，為校書郎。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and became Collator.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi and became a collator.

sentences.zh: 應制策科高等，授左拾遺，召入翰林為學士。

translations.literal: In the policy-examination curriculum he received high grade, was appointed Left Reminder, and was summoned into the Hanlin Academy as Academician.
translations.idiomatic: He ranked high in the policy examination, became Left Reminder, and entered the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 歲滿當改官，公輔上書自陳，以母老家貧，以府掾俸給稍優，乃求兼京兆尹戶曹參軍，特承恩顧。

translations.literal: When his term was full and he should have changed office, Gongfu submitted a memorial stating himself that his mother was old and the family poor; because the salary of a capital bureau aide was somewhat better, he therefore requested to hold concurrently the post of Registrar in the Household Bureau of the Metropolitan Prefect, especially receiving imperial favor.
translations.idiomatic: When due for promotion he asked instead to remain a metropolitan registrar for the better salary to support his aged mother, and the emperor granted it.

sentences.zh: 才高有器識，每對見言事，德宗多從之。

translations.literal: His talent was high and he had capacity and insight; whenever he spoke on affairs in audience, Dezong mostly followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Talented and far-sighted, he often advised Dezong, who usually followed his counsel.

sentences.zh: 建中四年十月，涇師犯闕。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the fourth year of Jianzhong the Jingzhou troops violated the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Jianzhong 4 (783) the Jingzhou mutiny broke out.

sentences.zh: 德宗蒼黃自苑北便門出幸，公輔馬前諫曰：「硃泚嘗為涇原帥，得士心。

translations.literal: Dezong in panic from the park's north convenient gate went out on tour; Gongfu before the horse remonstrated: 'Zhu Ci once was Military Governor of Jingyuan and won the soldiers' hearts.'
translations.idiomatic: Dezong fled through the park's north gate; Gongfu warned from horseback: "Zhu Ci once commanded Jingyuan and still commands the soldiers' loyalty."

sentences.zh: 昨以硃滔叛，坐奪兵權，泚常憂憤不得誌。

translations.literal: Yesterday because Zhu Tao rebelled he was deprived of military power by punishment; Ci always worried and resented that he could not achieve his aim.
translations.idiomatic: Because Zhu Tao rebelled, Ci was stripped of command, and he broods on the injustice.

sentences.zh: 不如使人捕之，使陪鑾駕，忽群兇立之，必貽國患。

translations.literal: It would be better to send men to seize him and have him accompany the imperial carriage; if suddenly the violent faction sets him up, it will surely leave a national calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Seize him and keep him with the imperial train; if the rebels proclaim him leader, calamity will follow.

sentences.zh: 臣頃曾陳奏，陛下茍不能坦懷待之，則殺之，養獸自貽其患，悔且無益。

translations.literal: Your servant once memorialized before: if Your Majesty cannot treat him with open heart, then kill him; to rear a beast is to bring disaster on oneself—regret will be of no use.'
translations.idiomatic: I have said before: if you cannot trust him openly, kill him; to spare a beast is to breed disaster."

sentences.zh: 」德宗曰：「已無及矣！

translations.literal: Dezong said: 'It is already beyond remedy!'
translations.idiomatic: Dezong replied: "It is too late!"

sentences.zh: 」從幸至奉天，拜諫議大夫，俄以本官同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Following the tour to Fengtian, he was appointed Remonstrating Grandee, and soon with his regular office made Fellow of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the court to Fengtian, became Remonstrating Grandee, then Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 從幸山南，車駕至城固縣，唐安公主薨。

translations.literal: Following the tour to Shannan, when the imperial carriage reached Chenggu County, Princess Tang'an died.
translations.idiomatic: On the flight to Shannan, Princess Tang'an died at Chenggu.

sentences.zh: 上之長女，昭德皇后所生，性聰敏仁孝，上所鐘愛。

translations.literal: The emperor's eldest daughter, born of Empress Zhaode, was by nature intelligent, filial, and kind, and the emperor especially cherished her.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's eldest daughter by Empress Zhaode was clever, filial, and dearly loved.

sentences.zh: 初，詔尚韋宥，未克禮會而遇播遷；

translations.literal: Earlier an edict had betrothed her to Wei You, but the rites could not be completed when the court was driven to wander.
translations.idiomatic: She had been betrothed to Wei You, but wedding rites were never completed before the flight.

sentences.zh: 及薨，上悲悼尤甚，詔所司厚其葬禮。

translations.literal: When she died the emperor's grief and mourning were especially deep; an edict ordered the relevant offices to make the funeral rites thick.
translations.idiomatic: At her death the emperor mourned deeply and ordered a lavish funeral.

sentences.zh: 公輔諫曰：「非久克復京城，公主必須歸葬，今於行路，且宜儉薄，以濟軍士。

translations.literal: Gongfu remonstrated: 'We have not long recovered the capital; the princess must be returned for burial; now on the road one should for the moment be frugal and thin, to aid the soldiers.'
translations.idiomatic: Gongfu urged: "We have not yet retaken Chang'an; the princess should be buried simply on the march to aid the troops."

sentences.zh: 」德宗怒，謂翰林學士陸贄曰：「唐安夭亡，不欲於此為塋壟，宜令造一磚塔安置，功費甚微，不合關宰相論列。

translations.literal: Dezong was angry and told Hanlin Academician Lu Zhi: 'Tang'an died young; I do not wish to make a mound here; it is fitting to order construction of one brick pagoda for placement—the labor cost is very slight; it should not concern the chief minister to discuss.'
translations.idiomatic: Dezong angrily told Lu Zhi: "I want only a small brick pagoda here—not a matter for the chief minister."

sentences.zh: 姜公輔忽進表章，都無道理，但欲指朕過失，擬自取名。

translations.literal: Jiang Gongfu suddenly submitted a memorial; it was wholly without principle, only wishing to point out my faults, intending to make a name for himself.'
translations.idiomatic: He fumed that Gongfu had memorialized only to criticize him and win a reputation.

sentences.zh: 朕比擢拔為腹心，乃負朕如此！

translations.literal: I recently promoted and pulled him up as a trusted intimate, yet he has betrayed me thus!
translations.idiomatic: I raised him as a trusted counselor, and this is how he repays me!

sentences.zh: 」贄對曰：「公輔官是諫議，職居宰衡，獻替固其職分。

translations.literal: Zhi replied: 'Gongfu's office is Remonstrating Grandee; his duty station is chief minister; offering replacement and correction is solidly his duty portion.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhi answered: "Gongfu is Remonstrating Grandee and chief minister; remonstrance is his duty."

sentences.zh: 本立輔臣，置之左右，朝夕納誨，意在防微，微而弼之，乃其所也。

translations.literal: The fundamental establishment of assisting ministers is to place them at left and right; morning and evening receiving admonition—the intent lies in guarding against the minute; when minute, to assist—is what is proper to them.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers are set at the ruler's side to admonish daily and check errors before they grow—that is their office.

sentences.zh: 陛下以造塔役費微小，非宰相所論之事。

translations.literal: Your Majesty takes the pagoda labor cost as minute—not a matter for the chief minister to discuss.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty thinks the pagoda a trifle beneath a chief minister's concern.

sentences.zh: 但問理之是非，豈論事之大小！

translations.literal: But one asks whether principle is right or wrong—how can one discuss whether the affair is large or small!
translations.idiomatic: Yet right and wrong matter, not the size of the affair!

sentences.zh: 若造塔為是，役雖大而作之何傷！

translations.literal: If building the pagoda is right, though the labor be great, what harm in doing it!
translations.idiomatic: If the pagoda is right, great expense does no harm.

sentences.zh: 若造塔為非，費雖小而言者何罪！

translations.literal: If building the pagoda is wrong, though the cost be small, what crime in speaking!
translations.idiomatic: If it is wrong, small expense does not make remonstrance a crime.

sentences.zh: 」帝又曰：「卿未會朕意。

translations.literal: The emperor again said: 'You have not understood my intent.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "You do not understand me."

sentences.zh: 朕以公輔才行，共宰相都不相當，在奉天時已欲罷免，後因公輔辭退，朕已面許。

translations.literal: I take Gongfu's talent and conduct together with the chief ministers—all are not suitable; at Fengtian I already wished to dismiss him; afterward because Gongfu resigned I already promised him to his face.'
translations.idiomatic: I find Gongfu unfit for the chief ministry; at Fengtian I meant to dismiss him, and when he resigned I promised it to his face.

sentences.zh: 尋屬懷光背叛，遂且因循，容至山南。

translations.literal: Soon it fell under Huai'guang's rebellion, so for the time being I went along, tolerating him until Shannan.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'guang's rebellion delayed matters, and I tolerated him through the flight to Shannan.

sentences.zh: 公輔知朕擬改官，所以固論造塔，賣直取名。

translations.literal: Gongfu knew I planned to change his office, so he firmly debated the pagoda, selling uprightness to make a name.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing I would demote him, he used the pagoda debate to pose as upright and win fame.

sentences.zh: 據此用心，豈是良善！

translations.literal: Judging by this intent, how is he good and kind!
translations.idiomatic: With such motives, how can he be called virtuous!

sentences.zh: 朕所惆悵者，只緣如此。

translations.literal: What I grieve over is only because of this.
translations.idiomatic: That is what grieves me.

sentences.zh: 」贄再三救護，帝怒不已，乃罷為左庶子。

translations.literal: Zhi repeatedly shielded and defended him; the emperor's anger did not cease, and he was dismissed to Left Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi pleaded for him in vain; the emperor dismissed Gongfu to Left Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 尋丁母憂，服闕，授右庶子，久之不遷。

translations.literal: Soon he entered mourning for his mother; when mourning ended he was appointed Right Mentor of the Heir Apparent, and for a long time was not transferred.
translations.idiomatic: He mourned his mother, then became Right Mentor, and long went without promotion.

sentences.zh: 洎陸贄知政事，以有翰林之舊，數告贄求官。

translations.literal: When Lu Zhi managed government affairs, because of old ties in the Hanlin Academy he several times told Zhi and sought office.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Zhi became chief minister, Gongfu, his old Hanlin colleague, repeatedly asked him for promotion.

sentences.zh: 贄密謂公輔曰：「予嘗見郴州竇相，言為公奏擬數矣，上旨不允，有怒公之言。

translations.literal: Zhi secretly told Gongfu: 'I once saw the Minister of Chenzhou, Dou, who said I have memorialized for you several times; the imperial intent did not approve, and there are words of anger toward you.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhi privately told him: "Dou Xiang of Chen said he had recommended him several times, but the emperor refused and spoke angrily of him."

sentences.zh: 」公輔恐懼，上疏乞罷官為道士，久之未報。

translations.literal: Gongfu was fearful and submitted a memorial begging to leave office and become a Daoist priest; for a long time there was no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Gongfu asked to resign and become a Daoist priest; no answer came for a long time.

sentences.zh: 後又廷奏，德宗問其故，公輔不敢泄贄，便以參言為對。

translations.literal: Later he again presented himself at court; Dezong asked the reason, and Gongfu did not dare reveal Zhi but took Can's words as his reply.
translations.idiomatic: Later he spoke in court; asked why, he dared not implicate Zhi and cited Dou Can instead.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，貶公輔為泉州別駕，又遣中使賫詔責竇參。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and demoted Gongfu to Assistant Prefect of Quanzhou, and also sent an inner envoy bearing an edict to reproach Dou Can.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor demoted Gongfu to assistant prefect in Quan and sent an envoy to rebuke Dou Can.

sentences.zh: 順宗即位，起為吉州刺史，尋卒。

translations.literal: When Shunzong took the throne, Gongfu was raised to Prefect of Jizhou and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shunzong he was made Prefect of Ji and soon died.

sentences.zh: 憲宗朝，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the Xianzong reign he was posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xianzong he was posthumously made Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：賈魏公以溫克長者，致位丞相，拒獻甫之請，畋李納之郊，則器略可知矣！

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Duke Jia of Wei, as a gentle and restrained elder, reached the post of chief minister; he refused Xianfu's request and hunted in Li Na's borderlands—then capacity and strategy may be known!
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Jia Dan, gentle and restrained, rose to chief minister; by refusing to kill Fan Ze and hunting in Li Na's territory he showed his magnanimity.

sentences.zh: 韋郢公慷慨節義，困於讒邪，命矣夫！

translations.literal: Duke Wei of Ying was generous in integrity and righteousness, trapped by slander and evil—such was fate!
translations.idiomatic: Wei Lun of Ying was generous and upright yet ruined by slander—such was fate!

sentences.zh: 趙丞相區分檢裁，求為雅士，以爭權而陷陸贄，則前時以德報怨，其可信乎！

translations.literal: Chief Minister Zhao distinguished and examined affairs, seeking to be an elegant gentleman; yet by contending for power he trapped Lu Zhi—then the earlier time of repaying enmity with virtue, can it be believed!
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Jing sought refinement, yet by power struggle he ruined Lu Zhi—so much for repaying injury with kindness.

sentences.zh: 公輔一言悟主，驟及臺司；

translations.literal: Gongfu with one word awakened the sovereign and suddenly reached the council seat.
translations.idiomatic: Gongfu with one word won the emperor and vaulted to the council.

sentences.zh: 一言不合，禮遽疏薄，則加膝墜泉之間，君道可知矣！

translations.literal: One word not in accord, ritual was suddenly thin and slight—then between adding to the knee and falling into the spring, the way of the ruler may be known!
translations.idiomatic: One word amiss, and favor vanished—between embrace and abyss the ruler's way is plain.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：元靖訏謨，真謂純儒。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Yuanjing's grand plans—truly called a pure Confucian.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says: Yuanjing's far-reaching counsel marked a true Confucian.

sentences.zh: 手調鼎飪，心運地圖。

translations.literal: With hand adjusting the tripod's stew, with heart turning the earth's maps.
translations.idiomatic: He seasoned the state's stew and charted the earth in his heart.

sentences.zh: 姜躁趙險，並躍天衢。

translations.literal: Jiang was rash, Zhao dangerous—both leaped the heavenly street.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang was impetuous, Zhao perilous—both soared then fell at court.

sentences.zh: 哀哉韋公，終困讒夫。

translations.literal: Alas, Duke Wei, in the end trapped by slanderers.
translations.idiomatic: Alas for Wei Lun, at last undone by slander.
